item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. item.content:encoded: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. Oregon head coach Dan Lanning talks to the defense during a timeout as the No. 13 Oregon Ducks face the No. 21 UCLA Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian “Everybody knows what we want to attack this next week, being that Nebraska is a good team,” he said. The outside noise has been deafening. To say that many Oregon fans have melted down on social media would be an understatement. Virtually all of the players have social media accounts. Moore said he is active on social media but ignores negativity. Finney said he isn’t very active on social media and doesn’t care what people say outside the program. “Why would I let your opinion inflict me or my thoughts on my performance or my thoughts on our performance,” he said. “Because people are going to be there when you’re doing good, when you’re bad; when you’re doing bad, they’re going to leave you.” For that reason, the team lives by the motto F.E.B.U., which stands for “Forget Everyone But Us”. “F.E.B.U. is a true statement that we all follow,” Finney said. “… Just back to work. We got to figure out what we did wrong, go to the doctor, and just get back to work.” Fifth-year linebacker Devon Jackson said before the season that his main goal was team-driven — winning the national title. He is no longer looking that far ahead. “At the end of the year, what happens, happens, but I promise if we focus on the day and focus on one game at a time, we will be okay,” Jackson said. On Saturday, the Ducks’ defense played one of its best games of the season, while the offense played its worst without starting quarterback Dante Moore , who remains in concussion protocol. On teams that lack closeness, such a contrast can cause issues. But that is not the case with Oregon. “I mean, we’re all in this together,” Jackson said. “It’s not like, the defense won the game and offense lost, or special teams won or lost. We all lost together and we all win together. So, we got each other’s back no matter what.” Oregon offensive players celebrate a touchdown run by running back Jordon Davison (#0) as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 UCLA Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Jackson said that after Saturday’s loss, he and senior center Iapani Laloulu talked for 20 minutes about the team. He told Laloulu that he didn’t care what was going on with the offense; the defense had its back. “I wouldn’t trade that group with anybody else in the country despite what other people may think,” Jackson said. “And we’re going to continue to lean on each other because it’s we all we got and we all we need.” Realistically, Oregon can’t expect much sympathy from outsiders. The Ducks have top-notch facilities, infinite uniform options, a roster with an estimated payroll of $50 million , and a coach who isn’t afraid to speak his mind, as Lanning did after beating the Trojans. Many in the football world certainly wouldn’t mind seeing Oregon fall. “Ain’t nobody going to feel sorry for us,” linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei said. “So just came back in the next day with the mindset ready to work.” . . . item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. Oregon Ducks QB Dylan Raiola (8) throws a pass to Oregon Ducks RB Dierre Hill Jr. (6) during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stad
item.content:encoded: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. Oregon Ducks QB Dylan Raiola (8) throws a pass to Oregon Ducks RB Dierre Hill Jr. (6) during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, IL. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire) (Icon Sportswire via AP Images) AP Raiola avoided throwing anyone under the bus but acknowledged what the question implied. Passing games are built on timing. If the quarterback can’t fully trust the receivers running the routes, synergy suffers and efficiency wanes. That’s less a knock on the receivers than an acknowledgment that it’s easier to develop a connection with a team’s more polished top receivers than with those thrust into action by circumstance. At times, running back Dierre Hill Jr. played wide receiver alongside freshmen Hudson Lewis and Gatlin Bair. Neither had played much until injuries hit the group. Lanning said Stewart would return. McClellan is out indefinitely. 5. The failed gadget play Much has been made about the failed gadget play in the third quarter. Many have blamed Mehringer for the play-call and the negative result hurting momentum. Let’s examine. Oregon trailed 14-10, forced an Illinois punt and took over at the Ducks’ 9-yard line. Five plays later, Oregon moved the ball to its 47. That’s when the gadget play came out. Oregon lined up with four offensive linemen to the far left, with wide receiver Dakorien Moore behind the linemen. Three Illinois defenders lined up on that side with a fourth closer to the box. Raiola checked to a run play and handed the ball to Moore on a jet sweep to the right, where the Ducks were outnumbered. The poorly-blocked play resulted in a one-yard loss. A couple of plays later, Oregon punted. After the game, Lanning was asked whether the failed play hurt the team at that moment. “Yeah, it’s a great question,” he said. “It certainly wasn’t successful. There’s a pause in operation there, right?” Yes, but who is at fault for the failed play? Is it Raiola for reading it wrong and not passing to Moore? Is it Mehringer for calling the play? Or is it Lanning for allowing the play to happen? For that play to be called, it must be accepted by Lanning, practiced, reviewed on film and further stamped by Lanning to appear on the play sheet. Then, when Mehringer calls it, Lanning must let it go through. He can hear every play call through the coaches’ headsets. If Lanning didn’t like the play, he could have vetoed it. He did not. The concept is not much different from when Lanning chooses to go for two after touchdowns. If Oregon gets the favorable look it wants, it takes the shot. That’s what happened with the gadget play. But Oregon made the wrong choice and the play failed. Regardless of the process, had Lanning not liked the play, he could have stopped it from being called. 6. Oregon’s rushing attack came to life Oregon gained 180 yards on the ground against a team that ranked 12th in the Big Ten in rushing defense, allowing 134.4 yards per game. CHAMPAIGN, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 24: Jordon Davison #0 of the Oregon Ducks scores a touchdown against Matthew Bailey #7 of Illinois during the first half at Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Champaign, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) Getty Images Still, too many drives started well before getting stuffed, putting more pressure on Raiola, who couldn’t consistently deliver. As a result, Oregon converted on just four of 15 third-down attempts. With most of the team’s top receivers out, the rushing attack needed to be special, and it wasn’t. 7. Tough day for kicker Gage Hurych The junior entered the game 9-for-9 on field-goal attempts and went 1-for-4. But two of his three misses came from beyond 50 yards. Hurych missed his first attempt from 52 yards out. He made a 20-yard field goal in the second quarter to put Oregon up 10-0. He missed a 53-yarder with 6:04 to go in the fourth quarter and later missed a 47-yarder with 52 seconds to go. “He’s human,” Lanning said. “The reality is, those are long kicks. Some of those are really tough. The wind’s a little bit different in this stadium. I think we put them in a position that wasn’t the easiest to operate, and we’ve been really fortunate this year.” 8. Rushing defense faltered when it mattered most. Oregon’s defense kept the Ducks in the games against UCLA and Nebraska until the offense started to come alive. Oregon lost to the Bruins 17-15 and beat Nebraska 17-14. On Saturday, the Ducks led 10-0 late in the second quarter. At that point, nobody knew Oregon wouldn’t score again. But the defense’s job was to keep dominating, just in case. Illinois Fighting Illini RB Aidan Laughery (21) runs the ball into the end zone for a touchdown during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, IL. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It failed. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. Michigan State Spartans defensive back Charles Brantley (4) tackles Illinois Fighting Illini wide receiver Collin Dixon (17) in a Big 10 football game at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, Mich. on Saturday, October 10, 2026. Isaac Ritchey | iritchey@mlive

(AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. Michigan State Spartans defensive back Charles Brantley (4) tackles Illinois Fighting Illini wide receiver Collin Dixon (17) in a Big 10 football game at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, Mich. on Saturday, October 10, 2026. Isaac Ritchey | iritchey@mlive.com “He knows he’s going to play now,” Lunney told reporters. But so too could Boyd. “We feel like we have another guy on campus in that room that can help us win and we’re very confident in that,” Bielema said. Oregon coach Dan Lanning said it’s difficult to scout Clayton given his limited body of work. Oregon has watched some of his high school game film. But mostly, Oregon will focus on Illinois’ system. “There might be wrinkles, but very rarely do people change the identity of their offense based on a change of the position,” Lanning said. “So you prepare and then you make sure you have answers for what you think that skill set is.” If Moore doesn’t return this week, Raiola and Thomas will compete for the starting job against Illinois. Raiola replaced Moore at USC and thrived in the win, but following a bye, struggled for three quarters during a 17-15 loss to UCLA on Oct. 10. Thomas performed better in the fourth quarter and almost pulled out the victory. Thomas started Saturday’s 17-14 home win over Nebraska, but struggled for three quarters before Lanning turned to Raiola. He led the Ducks from a 14-6 deficit to a win with a four-yard touchdown pass to tight end Jamari Johnson with 28 seconds remaining. Lanning said he’s confident in all four quarterbacks, including sophomore Akili Smith Jr., who had a play package ready for Nebraska if needed. Illinois is most familiar with Raiola, who, as a Nebraska freshman in 2024, passed for 297 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in a 31-24 overtime loss to Illinois. “Raiola is obviously a very accomplished player,” Bielema said. “Kind of almost unusual. You got to almost prepare for possibly three quarterbacks on Saturday. But we’ll kind of handle that during the course of the week and see where that goes.” . . . item.title: Dame Time is back in Portland — and the Blazers look dangerous
item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers’ coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game. What style will the Blazers play? In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. The roster is unbalanced, featuring five dynamic ball-handlers and playmakers (Lillard, Morant, Avdija, Holiday and Henderson), a solid center combination (Clingan and Williams) and little wing depth. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers’ coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game. What style will the Blazers play? In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. The roster is unbalanced, featuring five dynamic ball-handlers and playmakers (Lillard, Morant, Avdija, Holiday and Henderson), a solid center combination (Clingan and Williams) and little wing depth. As a result, the team is expected to play fast and free under Nori, bringing lots of speed, passing, cutting and flow. Nori said he hopes to rotate his players liberally in shorter shifts during games — perhaps as short as three minutes — which will enable them to play with maximum effort before giving way to teammates. The interior defense is strong with Clingan and Williams patrolling the middle, Camara remains one of the NBA’s best and most versatile defenders and Cissoko will be asked to guard one-through-five. Holiday is still capable of locking down opposing guards and Avdija has pledged to be more of a two-way threat now that he doesn’t have to serve as the team’s primary ball-handler. But the backcourt combination of Morant and Lillard, while lethal on offense, is not imposing on defense and relatively small (both stand 6-foot-2). What are the Blazers’ expectations? Portland defied pundits last season, winning 10 of its last 14 regular season games to secure a spot in the play-in tournament, where it beat the Suns in Phoenix to earn the seventh seed in the Western Conference. The San Antonio Spurs dismissed the Blazers with a gentleman’s sweep in the playoffs , but the strong run — combined with the additions of Lillard and Morant — has raised expectations in Portland. How much? Camara said in training camp that the Blazers’ goal is to win 50 or more games and secure home-court advantage in the postseason. It won’t be easy. The league is as deep and talented as ever, and new rules surrounding the lottery should discourage teams from tanking, meaning most of the league will be chasing wins instead of lottery ping-pong balls late into the season. It seemed like a third of the league had given up last year by the All-Star break. Latest Blazers news Joe Freeman’s 3 takeaways from the Trail Blazers’ back-to-back sweep vs. Thunder Trail Blazers lose rotation player for 2 months Joe Freeman’s 3 takeaways from Trail Blazers’ rout over the Thunder Thunder vs. Blazers predictions: Portland looks to snap two-game skid in the first of back-to-back meetings Joe Freeman’s 3 takeaways from Trail Blazers’ lopsided loss to Spurs Early-season schedule is a doozy As the Blazers’ new-look lineup works to build chemistry and a first-year coach settles into a new role, the schedule will be challenging. Six of the first eight games — and 12 of the first 17 — will come on the road and include a slew of playoff contenders, including the Spurs, Oklahoma City Thunder (twice), Minnesota Timberwolves (twice), New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers, Denver Nuggets and Los Angeles Lakers (twice). But what about Dame? The most uplifting part of opening night figures to be the return of Lillard, the franchise icon who is back after spending two seasons in Milwaukee and one season on the injured list. The nine-time All-Star and franchise leader has not played in an NBA regular-season or playoff game since April 27, 2025, when he suffered a torn left Achilles tendon. And he has not played with Portland since March 22, 2023, six months before it traded him to the Bucks. Lillard showed no ill effects from his injury during the exhibition season, when he played in three of the Blazers’ four games and averaged 17.3 points, 2.7 assists and 22.7 minutes. If anything, he looked like the same old Dame, swishing three-pointers, creating off the dribble, initiating offense and drawing defensive attention. Lillard joked earlier this week that he’s “not an old man,” but also acknowledged that he isn’t likely to play upward of 38 minutes a game like he used to and may even take a night off here and there for rest, most likely on a random back-to-back. His addition not only should help cover up two of the Blazers’ biggest weaknesses last season — three-point shooting and shooting in the clutch — but also inspire a thirsty fan base, which has rarely loved a player more. All the while, Lillard says he intends to play with more “joy” than ever. Read the original article on oregonlive.com . Add oregonlive.com as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They’re confident they can challenge any defense vertically. “The underneath throws are going to be there,” Hampton said. “We got the best OC in the country; we’re going to be able to go deep if we want to.” Latest Beavers news Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson going through further testing of hand injury before Boise State game Oregon State basketball lands 3-star center for 2027 class Oregon State wome

item.title: Braves sign former Dodgers relief pitcher Evan Phillips to contract
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers relief pitcher Evan Phillips celebrates after San Diego Padres' Wil Myers hit into a double play to end the top of the sixth inning in Game 1 of a baseball NL Division Series Tuesday, Oct. 11, 2022, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Marcio Jose Sanchez) The Atlanta Braves made their first move of Major League Baseball’s Winter Meetings on Thursday morning by adding a relief pitcher. The team signed reliever Evan Phillips to a 3-year, $35 million contract, adding him to what could be one of baseball’s best bullpens. [DOWNLOAD: Free WSB-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] The 32-year-old Phillips has been with Dodgers for the past 5 seasons. His 2026 season didn’t start until July after he recovered from Tommy John surgery in June of 2025. Phillips finished 2026 with a 3-2 record, a 3.46 ERA and 33 strikeouts. He pitched 5 times for the Dodgers during the playoffs and did not give up a single run. TRENDING STORIES: SEC Week 11: No. 1 Georgia hosts No. 22 Missouri while No. 8 Texas travels to No. 24 LSU 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup: US joint bid lists Atlanta as host city Georgia Bulldogs move to the top of the College Football Playoff rankings Phillips, who hails from Clayton, NC, was originally drafted by the Braves in the 17th round of the 2015 draft. He made it to Atlanta during the 2018 season, pitching in 4 games before being traded to Baltimore. He pitched for Tampa Bay in 2021 before landing with the Dodgers. [SIGN UP: WSB-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ] Phillips will team up with Robert Suarez, Dylan Lee and possibly Didier Fuentes to make a strong back end of the bullpen. Closer Raisel Iglesias is a free agent and it is not clear yet if he will return for another season.

item.title: NFL Week 10 preview & bold predictions: Joe Burrow vs. Aaron Rodgers, can Kirk Cousins save the Vikings?
item.description: Subscribe to Football 301 with Nate Tice Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube Nate Tice & Matt Harmon preview the biggest games of Week 10 of the NFL season. The duo start off by deep diving on their three favorite games: the New England Patriots & Detroit Lions battling in Munich, the Pittsburgh Steelers & Cincinnati Bengals in a Sunday night hoss fight and the San Francisco 49ers & Dallas Cowboys facing off in what could be a barn burner. Later, Nate & Matt give one key thing to watch in the Houston Texans vs. Cleveland Browns game (including one very clear path C.J. Stroud can use to dominate the Browns defense) and the Minnesota Vikings battling the Green Bay Packers in Kirk Cousins’ return to the purple. The guys wrap up with their Hail Mary bold predictions for the weekend, including a big game from Derrick Henry on Monday night and a tight end fest between the Los Angeles Rams & Arizona Cardinals (plus expectations for Fernando Mendoza’s first start for the Las Vegas Raiders). item.title: After World Cup experience, Leo Nannetti shares lessons with Brazil U20s
item.description: After World Cup experience, Leo Nannetti shares lessons with Brazil U20s Brazil’s youth national teams are the natural pathway to the senior side. Goalkeeper Leo Nannetti, however, landed a golden ticket and got a “sneak peek” at life with the Seleção during the 2026 World Cup, when he was invited to join the squad and had the privilege of training alongside his idols. Now he is putting that experience to work with the U-20s and sharing what he learned with his teammates. Nannetti’s first opportunity with Brazil came with the U-17 national team in 2024, when he played in the Cascais Luso Cup. In 2025, however, he skipped a step: he joined the senior squad for training at Granja Comary ahead of World Cup qualifiers against Chile and Bolivia. In 2026, the invitation was like a VIP pass: he attended the World Cup and trained alongside Alisson, Ederson and Weverton under Taffarel’s guidance, experiencing the tournament atmosphere firsthand. Leo Nannetti: U-17 call-ups and invitations to train with the senior national team already on his résumé, and now looking forward to a tournament with the U-20s Credits: Joilson Marconne / CBF “I never imagined I would be experiencing a World Cup atmosphere at 18. It added so much to my career and my personal life. I was alongside my idols, watching how they conduct themselves, how they train and how they prepare for each game. I’ll carry that experience with me for the rest of my life,” he said. Naturally, these experiences spark curiosity among his teammates, although most already play for their clubs’ senior teams. Nannetti shares what he can and draws on the experience he has gained throughout his career to keep improving with Brazil’s U-20s. The goalkeeper has been working hard in training in Belém ahead of two friendlies against Peru Credits: Joilson Marconne / CBF “A lot of them ask what it was like, and I always try to answer as naturally as possible. The technical and mental demands change a lot from one national team to the next. The U-17s are more about development, the U-20s are very competitive, and the senior team—well, that goes without saying, doesn’t it? The pressure they carry, representing an entire nation,” he said. The goalkeeper considers one thing essential: keeping each of these experiences in perspective so he can continue developing. “I always try to keep my feet on the ground. If I’m here today, I have God, coach Paulo Victor and the coaching staff to thank for believing in my work. And I have to remember that being called up now doesn’t mean I’ll be at the South American Championship. It’s an important step, but I give my best in every training session to try to secure my place in the squad,” he concluded. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: NHL rumors: Insider floats Jason Robertson-Nikita Kucherov blockbuster trade
item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images NHL rumors: Insider floats Jason Robertson-Nikita Kucherov blockbuster trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Neither Nikita Kucherov nor Jason Robertson is under contract beyond the 2026-27 season. With Kucherov having requested a trade and the Dallas Stars expected to revisit extension talks with Robertson in December, Daily Faceoff’s Matt Larkin floated a hypothetical blockbuster : the Tampa Bay Lightning and Stars swapping their star forwards one for one. “It’s difficult to imagine (Robertson) and the Stars getting in bed together long-term after such contentious negotiations,” Larkin wrote in his latest NHL Trade Board. “But they need him this season; it only makes sense to trade him if it’s in a hockey deal that helps them now. “How about Kucherov, one for one?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lightning general manager Julien BriseBois has said he doesn’t intend to trade Kucherov, but keeping him without an extension risks losing him for nothing next summer. Kucherov has been on a tear since his trade request, amassing 11 points in six games. He’s certainly not quiet quitting on the team where he won two Stanley Cups, but his future in Tampa remains in doubt. “As much as Kucherov and his camp might feel content to play out the season in Tampa, it remains to be seen if it will make things uncomfortable in the room, and it won’t stop suitors from coming forward with offers,” Larkin added. “That’s why Kucherov lands in tier 1 of this list. It’s tough to imagine this saga dragging all the way to July 1, even if his camp is fine with that happening.” Kucherov continues to be one of the NHL’s best players, now at 26 points in 18 games, while Robertson is off to another great start for the Stars, with nine goals and 19 points of his own in 17 games. Robertson’s name has been swirling in trade rumors for over a year. He reportedly turned down an eight-year offer worth about $15 million annually from the Seattle Kraken in a proposed sign-and-trade. He ended up inking a one-year, $12 million pact with Dallas to avoid arbitration, but his future remains up in the air. Both Dallas and Tampa Bay remain Stanley Cup contenders, so any deal would have to help them win now. A one-for-one swap seems unlikely, but crazier things have happened in the NHL. Related: NHL rumors: Maple Leafs looking for blue line help on trade market Related: Best Matvei Michkov landing spots amid growing trade buzz

item.title: Microsoft Outlook is down
item.description: Over the last hour or so, reports have come in from around the world that people can't access their Outlook email, either through the web or apps. Microsoft has acknowledged the issue from its Microsoft 365 Status account , saying that "We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors." There were also some reports of problems with Teams, but some of the people reporting issues say Teams is still working now. item.title: COP31: African youths map water challenges in 51 countries, seek greater role in policy decisions
item.description: In Nigeria, the 2024 Demographic and Health Survey found that 71 per cent of the population had access to at least basic drinking water services. However, only 38 per cent of households had water on their premises, while 66 per cent had sufficient quantities when needed The post COP31: African youths map water challenges in 51 countries, seek greater role in policy decisions appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .

item.title: NFL analyst picks Bears’ Caleb Williams over NFC North rivals for playoff run
item.description: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has earned another vote of confidence ahead of the next NFL playoff race. ESPN analyst Evan Cohen picked Williams over his NFC North rivals when asked which quarterback he trusted most in a postseason situation. Speaking on ESPN’s First Take, Shae Cornette asked Cohen which division quarterback he would trust in a playoff game. Cohen chose Williams despite acknowledging the experience and recent form of his competition. “I’m going to answer it. The answer is Caleb Williams,” Cohen said. “Even though Jared Goff is the one who’s been there and done that.” MORE: Giants’ J.J. McCarthy shares honest reaction to Kirk Cousins’ Vikings return Cohen also praised Jordan Love, noting that the Packers quarterback was “probably playing better than anyone else right now.” He also mentioned Kirk Cousins, saying, “a quarterback that is unbelievably experienced.” His choice stands out because Chicago faces strong competition from Detroit’s Jared Goff and Green Bay’s Jordan Love. Both quarterbacks have delivered more consistent production this season. Goff has completed 67.8% of his passes for 2,134 yards, 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. Love leads the division with 2,618 passing yards and 19 touchdowns. Williams has completed 68.7% of his passes for 1,546 yards, eight touchdowns and five interceptions. He has also added 145 rushing yards and two scores across six games. Caleb Williams has earned trust despite mistakes Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) reacts after the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Despite the Bears quarterback’s struggles, Cohen sees something different in Williams. “I just think Caleb Williams has got that effect,” he explained. “And I believe in his coach and his connection with his coach. I also believe that there’s a guy with big orange sleeves on defense and Jeffrey Simmons that is going to make Caleb Williams’ life easier by being so great on defense.” Cohen’s confidence comes despite Williams’ turnover problems during Chicago’s recent playoff run. The quarterback threw two interceptions against Green Bay before delivering a dramatic comeback victory. He completed 24 of 48 passes for 361 yards and two touchdowns in the 31-27 Wild Card win. Williams also helped Chicago force overtime against the Rams, throwing a late touchdown to Cole Kmet. However, three interceptions contributed to the Bears’ 20-17 defeat. Recently, Williams committed four interceptions in a 27-24 win over Tampa Bay. Still, Cohen viewed his resilience as a positive. “I will trust Caleb Williams in a big spot. And yes, we’re coming off of a four-turnover game for him, five for the team, but that actually makes me more impressed. They still won,” he said, referring to the game. "The answer is Caleb Williams. … Caleb Williams has got that 'IT' factor." @EvCoRadio weighs in on

item.title: Folarin Balogun and Sebastian Berhalter speak out on Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT impact and future
item.description: Folarin Balogun and Sebastian Berhalter spoke with reporters about head coach Mauricio Pochettino on Thursday -Credit:Cory Knowlton/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images As things stand, it is widely expected that after little more than two years in charge of the U.S. Men’s National Team, head coach Mauricio Pochettino is set to move back to the Premier League to take charge of a wayward Manchester United. While neither U.S. Soccer, United, nor Pochettino have yet confirmed this, it is believed that the 54-year-old will remain with the USMNT for the duration of their ongoing camp , including their two upcoming CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final games against Haiti, before jetting off to Manchester. And while the U.S. players are fully aware of what is being reported, it appears that they are equally unaware of whether or not Pochettino’s time in charge is coming to a swift end for certain. Balogun confirmed that the players have yet to find out if Pochettino's supposedly impending move to Manchester United is a sure thing -Credit:Alex Livesey - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images Speaking with reporters on Thursday, striker Folarin Balogun said, “Obviously, we see everything that's being written online as something we can't avoid as players. “But, me speaking personally, I don't know if it's true, if it's not, if it's confirmed. My only focus is just to come into practice and prepare for the games. And I'm sure if it is something that does become official, he'll let us know as soon as possible.” This sentiment was echoed by midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, son of Pochettino’s predecessor Gregg, who commented, “We're focused on going against Haiti twice. They're a good team. And I think you saw that World Cup. They surprised people. So that's our main focus. And yeah, I think the group is ready to play these games.” Should this camp prove Pochettino’s last with the USMNT, despite having signed a four-year deal following this past summer’s FIFA World Cup where they were knocked out by Belgium in the Round of 16, the impact the former Tottenham Hotspur boss has had will seemingly stick around. “Personally, on the field and off the field, he's done a lot for me,” Berhalter said. “And, I think from day one, he's always believed in me before I set foot on the field. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE “I think just the way I play and the way that I try to carry myself. I think he just said, ‘Doesn't matter what you're doing on the field, these are already the right things.’ And to be honest, I can't thank him enough for - regardless if he's the coach, [or] not the coach. “And I think I say it every time that he's meant so much to me. While neither U.S. Soccer, United, nor Pochettino have yet confirmed this, it is believed that the 54-year-old will remain with the USMNT for the duration of their ongoing camp , including their two upcoming CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final games against Haiti, before jetting off to Manchester. And while the U.S. players are fully aware of what is being reported, it appears that they are equally unaware of whether or not Pochettino’s time in charge is coming to a swift end for certain. Balogun confirmed that the players have yet to find out if Pochettino's supposedly impending move to Manchester United is a sure thing -Credit:Alex Livesey - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images Speaking with reporters on Thursday, striker Folarin Balogun said, “Obviously, we see everything that's being written online as something we can't avoid as players. “But, me speaking personally, I don't know if it's true, if it's not, if it's confirmed. My only focus is just to come into practice and prepare for the games. And I'm sure if it is something that does become official, he'll let us know as soon as possible.” This sentiment was echoed by midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, son of Pochettino’s predecessor Gregg, who commented, “We're focused on going against Haiti twice. They're a good team. And I think you saw that World Cup. They surprised people. So that's our main focus. And yeah, I think the group is ready to play these games.” Should this camp prove Pochettino’s last with the USMNT, despite having signed a four-year deal following this past summer’s FIFA World Cup where they were knocked out by Belgium in the Round of 16, the impact the former Tottenham Hotspur boss has had will seemingly stick around. “Personally, on the field and off the field, he's done a lot for me,” Berhalter said. “And, I think from day one, he's always believed in me before I set foot on the field. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE “I think just the way I play and the way that I try to carry myself. I think he just said, ‘Doesn't matter what you're doing on the field, these are already the right things.’ And to be honest, I can't thank him enough for - regardless if he's the coach, [or] not the coach. “And I think I say it every time that he's meant so much to me. And he's helped me develop as a player and as a person. And as a player, that's all you can ask for, to have that trust and have that belief in you. And for me, it's easy to go out there and just do my job. So he's meant a good deal to me, for sure.” From a broader perspective, both Balogun and Berhalter praised the “standard” and “environment” Pochettino has established within the USMNT, with the latter suggesting that some of the Argentine’s fire has enhanced their own pride to represent the Stars and Stripes. “I think we all know what we're expected and we're always working 100%, we're always fighting, we're always doing the little things to make sure we're representing this country in the right way,” he said. “And I think he really instilled that in us. Even though he's an Argentinian coach, he made us even more proud to be American, and I think that it speaks volumes of who he is as a person and as a coach.” • Mauricio Pochettino's USMNT and Manchester United future becomes clear • Ex-MLS star tears into Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT tenure ahead of Manchester United move The Middlesbrough star went on to note that regardless of whether or not Pochettino sticks around, he does not anticipate any of this will change moving forward. “I think the benefit and the blessing when you have a great coach is you know the standard,” AS Monaco's Balogun later said. “I think Poch has definitely raised the standard since he's been in charge. I think you guys have seen that just the intensity of training, how we approach games, he's changed our way of thinking as players from calling the friendlies that we have in certain camps - official games [or] not official games. “He wants us to just be of a mindset to go out there and win. I think he's laid the foundation, and I think us as players have that ownership to not just do that because Poch was in charge, I think we have the ownership as players to carry that out because we know the standard. “So yeah, I think that's the benefit of having a top coach. And I'm sure, whether he's here, whether he's not, the U.S. will look to replace him with another top coach.” Exactly who could replace Pochettino remains to be seen, although it has been reported that U.S. Soccer is keen to attempt to lure Pep Guardiola out of his break from coaching.

item.title: ‘I Still Talk to Him’: Aaron Rodgers Looks Forward to Reuniting with Mike Tomlin on Sunday Night
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike Tomlin after the Steelers' 34-32 win over the New York Jets on Sept. 7, 2025. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has tuned in to watch Mike Tomlin on NBC’s Football Night in America this season. He thinks his former head coach is a natural as an analyst. “I’m not surprised in the least,” Rodgers said of Tomlin turning heads in his new role. “He is absolutely killing it on TV the few times I’ve seen him. Nobody can talk football better than Mike T, so it is an absolute match made in heaven. Him being on TV and doing what he does. And I don’t know if he still wants to coach at some point, but he’s doing a hell of a job.” Tomlin will see his former team up close and in person for the first time on Sunday night since resigning in January. “I look forward to it because of the relationships, but you know me, I’m capable of compartmentalizing, and getting hyper-focused on the job,” Tomlin said on a conference call with NBC Sports on Wednesday. “But it certainly will be fun to see some guys I got relationships with and there’ll certainly be a lot of those. But they have a job to do, I have a job to do, and so I’m sure everyone’s going to be focused on the task at hand.” Rodgers still keeps in touch with Tomlin. “I still talk to him,” Rodgers said. “I love Mike T, and I have so much appreciation for him bringing me here last year and the amount of fun that we had together. The closeness of the bond that we formed. So it’ll be good to see him.” “I’m having a lot of fun,” Tomlin said. “Haven’t given one iota of thought about coaching. I’m sure that some of that’s going to come up in the not-too-distant future. But I’ll cross that bridge when I come to it. Really haven’t thought a lot about it. Really excited about my new role and working to get better each and every week.” Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy has never seen Tomlin smile more than he is right now. “I’m really happy for Mike. I’m trying not to laugh because I’ve never seen him smile so much. I’m told he’s very happy. He’s doing a great job. So I definitely hope to run into him there in Cincinnati,” McCarthy said. Alan Saunders provided reporting from Pittsburgh. item.title: Harry Kane breaks England appearance record and presented with gifts ahead of Croatia clash
item.description: Harry Kane has broken Peter Shilton ’s appearance record for the England men’s team after playing against Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley this evening. Thomas Tuchel had already confirmed at his pre-match press conference on Wednesday that his captain Kane would start the match and that was rubber-stamped when the teams were released an hour and 15 minutes before kick-off. It is the 33-year-old’s first game for his country since winning the Ballon d’Or last month and will be his record 126th England cap, meaning he surpasses Shilton atop the list. Harry Kane broke the England appearance record (PA) The legendary goalkeeper presented Kane – who has also scored a record 91 goals for the Three Lions – with a special golden crest ahead of the match at Wembley to celebrate the milestone. During the short ceremony ahead of kick-off, Kane was given a replica of the ball that Englishmen brought to Croatia in 1880 to start their love affair with football. That was presented by Croatia captain Luka Modric. Prince William also presented Kane with a framed England shirt with ‘Kane 126’ on the back before the English trio posed for photos. Harry Kane, Prince William and Peter Shilton all were involved in the pre-match celebration (Reuters) Kane was also re-presented with hi Ballon d’Or trophy (PA) Kane was then re-presented with his Ballon d’Or trophy after last month’s triumph as the crowd saluted their hero and unfurled a huge tifo of the striker. The Independent’s chief sports writer Lawrence Ostlere was at Wembley and said: “A nice moment here at Wembley to mark Harry Kane’s extraordinary career, with his children on the pitch. The highlight was undoubtedly Prince William ushering Peter Shilton to come and join in the group photo with Kane, like a very weird family holiday.” It was an emotional and celebratory atmosphere for the man who many consider to be England’s greatest player of all-time. England boss Tuchel wrote in his programme notes: “It’s the perfect place to celebrate Harry Kane and his recent achievements. There’s something quite poetic about the fact that almost a week or so after he was named England’s first Ballon d’Or winner for over 25 years, he’s now on the cusp of becoming the country’s all-time record caps holder. It’s so special not just for Harry but for all of us. “He has had a very special few weeks and the scary thing is, he is getting better and better, and even more influential. Winning the Ballon d’Or and becoming the all-time appearance record holder are both huge achievements, and I think it’s really important that he gets to celebrate these moments in front of our fans – because everyone should be proud. “Harry is humble, and he is very aware that everything is a team effort. He is a true leader and a true team player, which makes our number nine very special. So, he deserves all the credit, and hopefully he keeps on doing what he does best… scoring goals for us.” Kane won the Ballon d’Or last month (AFP/Getty) Eng

item.title: Texans vs. Browns Week 10 picks: Cleveland being treated like an afterthought
item.description: The Cleveland Browns take on the Houston Texans this Sunday. The Browns are 3-0 at home this year, but after having lost two straight games, they are being treated like an afterthought this week. As you can see in the national picks below, not a single person is picking the Browns at home. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 10 game between the Browns and Texans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Texans: Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley’s unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers’ league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who’s allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud’s other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston’s lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns’ permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans’ team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Texans 21, Browns 20 This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won’t matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that’s going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he’ll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That’s a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Texans 20, Browns 17 The Texans hope to sneak back into the playoff picture and their defense got back to making big plays in Los Angeles after the bye. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley’s unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers’ league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who’s allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud’s other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston’s lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns’ permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans’ team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Texans 21, Browns 20 This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won’t matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that’s going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he’ll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That’s a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Texans 20, Browns 17 The Texans hope to sneak back into the playoff picture and their defense got back to making big plays in Los Angeles after the bye. Cleveland’s defense will get a break as Houston is one-dimensional out of necessity, but in the end, old Texans friend Deshaun Watson will be outdueled by red-hot C.J. Stroud. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Texans 22, Browns 19 Shedeur Sanders had 297 passing yards and two TDs in his first start of the season, and that might be enough to keep that in a home start against the Texans. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD performance against the Chargers. The Browns’ early-season shine is wearing off, but they are 4-0 ATS as an underdog of seven points or less. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger, who has 25 tackles the last two weeks, helps Cleveland stick around at home. Below are our Week 10 NFL staff picks:

item.title: Braves Sign Evan Phillips To $35 Million Deal Eight Years After Trading Him Away
item.description: Atlanta Braves pitcher Evan Phillips The Atlanta Braves have made the first big splash in free agency by signing former Los Angeles Dodgers reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal. The Braves announced in a press release that Phillips will make $11 million in 2027 and 2028, and $13 million in 2029. He will also donate 1% of his salary to the Atlanta Braves Foundation. The Braves originally drafted Phillips in the 2015 MLB Draft, and he made his MLB debut with them in 2018. He was traded to the Baltimore Orioles that same year in a deal that landed the Braves Kevin Gausman and Darren O'Day. Since then, he has also played for the Tampa Bay Rays and the Los Angeles Dodgers. He has been with the Dodgers since 2021 and has been key in their success. Since joining the Dodgers, he has posted a 2.36 ERA in 232 games. From 2022-2024, he pitched in 187 games with a 2.21 ERA and notched 44 saves. In 2025, he underwent Tommy John surgery and did not return until July of last season. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Last season, he ended up pitching in 31 regular-season games with a 3.46 ERA. He also threw three scoreless innings in the postseason. Phillips is 32 years old and still has some good baseball left in him. The Braves won't need him to close games, as they already have Robert Suárez, who is very capable of closing games if Raisel Iglesias leaves in free agency. If Iglesias does return, the Braves will have an even better bullpen than last season, with Phillips now in the mix as well. Phillips won the World Series with the Dodgers in 2024, throwing 6 2/3 scoreless innings in the postseason. He was injured for the World Series run in 2025, however. More MLB: Braves Gold Glover Reportedly Drawing Interest From Dodgers

item.title: Sophie Cunningham names the LA Lakers player she should be compared to instead of Luka Doncic
item.description: Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images WNBA star Sophie Cunningham instantly distanced herself from a statistical comparison to Luka Doncic, and pointed the conversation in another direction. Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham discussed the Los Angeles Lakers on the latest episode of the No Hesitation podcast. Luka Doncic is averaging a stunning 38.6 ppg this season for the Western Conference leaders, putting himself in the MVP conversation. To point out just how prolific Doncic’s scoring streak is, podcast host Drew Hanlen pointed out that he is attempting almost as many shots this season as Sophie Cunningham did the entire WNBA season, and has already overtaken her for free-throws. He said: “Through his first nine games, he has attempted 221 shots. Last season in 43 games, you attempted 226 shots, so he is five behind you this season…. The second thing is, Luka has attempted 102 free throws already after nine games, and last season you attempted 74.” Sophie Cunningham asks for fairer comparison Sophie Cunningham pointed out that Luka Doncic makes a huge amount more money than she does. And instead, she asked to be compared to another Los Angeles Lakers players who she shares a more similar level of production with. She said: “And I also think you’re missing a big one: he also makes $50 million a year. I make $700,000 on my WNBA check. “You should compare me more to Quentin Grimes, we average around eight to 10 points, I think that’s it. My three-point shooting is actually better than the both of them. So if we’re going to compare, let’s compare.” It should be pointed out that Quentin Grimes is coming off the bench this season for the Lakers. His best season averaged was in 2024-25 where he posted 14.6ppg split across his spells with the Dallas Mavericks and Philadelphia 76ers. His 28-game spell exclusively with the Sixers saw him post 21.9 ppg. Sophie Cunningham’s best scoring WNBA regular season was in 2022 with the Phoenix Mercury, where she averaged 12.6 points per game. Grimes is making $13.9m with the Lakers this season as part of a four-year $60m deal signed in the offseason.

item.title: Predicting Big Ten football scores in Week 11: USC could feel Indiana’s wrath
item.description: It’s been a wild season of college football and that has a lot to do with the Big Ten . Through 10 weeks, it would’ve been hard to imagine Ohio State, Michigan , and Penn State not having much of a shot at winning the Big Ten. The Buckeyes are technically still alive, but Ohio State would need a lot to go its way to win the conference. Right now, UCLA remains unbeaten and Indiana is in second with one loss. The Hoosiers have looked mortal in recent weeks, but the playoff committee might’ve made the mistake by dropping Indiana on its bye week — Curt Cignetti has found his bulletin board material. The Hoosiers will host USC, which is the big game of the week. Oregon is still fully alive , despite having three total losses. With two Big Ten losses, the Ducks could win out and have a couple of things go their way and make the Big Ten Championship Game. Here’s how all the games could go down. MORE : College Football Playoff winners & losers: Indiana massive loser entering Week 11 No. 18 USC vs. No. 9 Indiana Indiana Head Coach Curt Cignetti during the Indiana versus Northwestern football game at Memorial Stadium on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Just when USC was starting to figure something out, it had to take a bye week, but that isn’t the worst part for Lincoln Riley. It’s that the Trojans have to play Indiana, which got slighted in the latest College Football Playoff rankings after also having a bye week. Curt Cignetti will use the Hoosiers dropping four spots after not playing as motivation for his team. It’s no secret that Indiana hasn’t played well. The Hoosiers could very easily have more than one loss. Teams like Northwestern, Michigan, Nebraska, and Minnesota all had chances to beat IU. But Indiana had a week to get healthy and Cignetti will be ready. If USC has any shot here, the Trojans have to play good defense and hope Jayden Maiava doesn’t turn the ball over. Final score: Indiana 31, USC 2 1 The rest of the games will be quick-hitter style: No. 4 UCLA 27, Illinois 20 No. 20 Ohio State 24, Northwestern 14 Wisconsin 34, Maryland 27 Nebraska 31, Rutgers 13 No. 16 Oregon 24, Michigan 10 Washington 24, Michigan State 14 Penn State 31, Minnesota 24 No. 15 Iowa 31, Purdue 13 — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: 'College GameDay' Week 11 location is a curious choice
item.description: ESPN's "College GameDay" will be having a change of pace for its Week 11 show. The GameDay crew is headed to the Pac-12 for a showdown between the No. 24 Boise State Broncos and the Oregon State Beavers . GameDay has not attended a Pac-12 game since 2023. The revamped conference is hoping to land a bid as the highest-ranked non-Power Four team in the College Football Playoff. Currently, Boise State is projected to land that spot. Based on the current rankings, Boise State would be the No. 12 seed in the playoff. GameDay has not attended Boise, Idaho, since the Broncos hosted Oregon State back in 2010 . GameDay picked the Oregon State at Boise State game over other top Nov. 14 matchups including Missouri at Georgia , Wake Forest at SMU, USC at Indiana, Michigan at Oregon, Texas at LSU, Utah at Arizona and Texas Tech at Oklahoma State. Boise State's top competition to land the non-Power Four playoff bid includes New Mexico, North Texas and Liberty. The Boise State game will be GameDay's first trip to a non-Power Four destination since attending James Madison's campus in 2023. "Get ready Boise we're coming to your city! GameDay announced via social media. "We're heading west for a Pac-12 showdown that could have CFP implications between Oregon State and Boise State." The Georgia-Missouri is GameDay's last legitimate chance to come to Athens during the regular season. We doubt GameDay would come to Georgia for the Georgia Tech game on rivalry week since Georgia Tech has had an awful season. GameDay has not come to Athens since the Ole Miss game in Oct. 2025. The last year where GameDay did not come to Athens was in 2018. College GameDay locations in 2026 Week 1: Clemson at LSU (Baton Rouge, Louisiana) Week 2: Ohio State at Texas (Austin, Texas) Week 3: LSU at Ole Miss (Oxford, Mississippi) Week 4: Texas at Tennessee (Knoxville, Tennessee) Week 5: Ohio State at Iowa (Iowa City, Iowa) Week 6: Georgia at Alabama (Tuscaloosa, Alabama) Week 7: Notre Dame at BYU (Provo, Utah) Week 8: Houston at Utah (Salt Lake City, Utah) Week 9: Minnesota at Indiana (Bloomington, Indiana) Week 10: Miami at Notre Dame (South Bend, Indiana) Week 11: Oregon State at Boise State (Boise, Idaho) GameDay settles on Week 11 location GET READY BOISE, WE'RE COMING TO YOUR CITY‼️ We're heading west for a Pac-12 showdown that could have CFP implications between Oregon State and Boise State 🍿 pic.twitter.com/o9XzuwoKyv — College GameDay (@CollegeGameDay) November 8, 2026 Follow UGA Wire on Instagram , Facebook , X (formerly Twitter) or Threads for more college football coverage! This article originally appeared on UGA Wire: 'College GameDay' Week 11 location is a curious choice
