item.title: FIFA fails to stop UEFA disclosure order over World Cup investor plan
item.description: FILE PHOTO - FIFA's logo is seen at FIFA headquarters ahead of the draw ceremony for the 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Zurich. (is associated with: «FIFA fails to stop UEFA disclosure order over World Cup investor plan») Christian Charisius/dpa A New York court has thrown out world football governing body FIFA's application to stop European football ruling body UEFA’s disclosure order against Thrive Capital and JP Morgan surrounding the doomed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal. FIFA president Gianni Infantino had sought to set up FFE to run the commercial interests of the World Cup and its other competitions, with private investors holding a minority stake, although the plan was abandoned in August after being rejected by three continental confederations. UEFA initially threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions, and Europe’s governing body last month demanded answers to a series of questions about FFE and a range of other concerns about Infantino’s presidency. The letter posed questions around the decision to award exclusivity to Thrive Capital to lead the FFE private investor group. Thrive was founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law JP Morgan was also confirmed by FIFA to be working alongside it on the FFE plan, having also been involved as financial backers for the doomed European Super League project in 2021. Thursday’s ruling in Manhattan means FIFA’s motion to intervene has been denied, but it is understood there needs to be another court decision to grant the disclosure of documents. Judge Jeannette Vargas wrote: “The court has already decided that the US FIFA parties have no direct, substantial and legally protectable interest in the subject matter of this application." “In light of this determination, the court exercises its discretion to decline leave to intervene,” Vargas added. The Press Association has contacted FIFA and UEFA for comment.

item.title: 2027: ‘Arrest perpetrators’, Senate condemns political violence nationwide
item.description: By Henry Umoru AHEAD of 2027 Presidential and general elections, the Senate has condemned in very strong terms, cases of political violence, attacks and disruption of political activities across the country. The Senate has thus taken a swipe at acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political rallies, meetings, processions and other lawful political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected. The Senate has urged the security agents to as a matter of urgency apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act in order to serve as deterrent to others. The Upper Chamber has called on all political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies in maintaining public peace. Speaking with Vanguard yesterday, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Media and Public Affairs, Senator Yemi Adaramodu, APC, Ekiti South, said, “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is preaching peace and national harmony, the National Assembly is in support of Mr President on this. “We thus condemn in totality any act of political violence and urge the security agents to apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act.” Vanguard News The post 2027: ‘Arrest perpetrators’, Senate condemns political violence nationwide appeared first on Vanguard News .
item.dc:creator: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com

item.title: Inside Bryson DeChambeau's surprising New England golf adventure
item.description: Bryson DeChambeau at Sugarloaf. Bryson DeChambeau / YT This week, Rory McIlroy was asked a version of a question that’s been bouncing around the golf world for months? What’s Bryson DeChambeau going to do next? The question was specifically about the possibility of DeChambeau playing the DP World Tour in 2027. “Honestly, look, I’m certainly not in his shoes, nor would I ever want to be,” McIlroy said. “But it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options. You know, if he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options.” That first line was a shot at his rival. That second line was tough but true; DeChambeau’s hopes of helping launch LIV 2.0 seem kaput, and he’s still suspended from the PGA Tour. But McIlroy’s third line was an acknowledgement that if, in fact, DeChambeau’s career aspirations are not bound by the traditional limits of professional golf tours — he has plenty of options indeed. Which is why, as LIV’s bankruptcy rolled on and DeChambeau’s ex-coworkers released statements about their futures, DeChambeau remained quiet, before ending up somewhere nobody expected: Western Maine. (You can listen to a version of this story on the Drop Zone podcast below or here .) “ SUGARLOAF IS ONE OF THOSE HIDDEN-AWAY PLACES,” says Oscar Park, the course’s head professional. item.content:encoded: Bryson DeChambeau at Sugarloaf. Bryson DeChambeau / YT This week, Rory McIlroy was asked a version of a question that’s been bouncing around the golf world for months? What’s Bryson DeChambeau going to do next? The question was specifically about the possibility of DeChambeau playing the DP World Tour in 2027. “Honestly, look, I’m certainly not in his shoes, nor would I ever want to be,” McIlroy said. “But it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options. You know, if he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options.” That first line was a shot at his rival. That second line was tough but true; DeChambeau’s hopes of helping launch LIV 2.0 seem kaput, and he’s still suspended from the PGA Tour. But McIlroy’s third line was an acknowledgement that if, in fact, DeChambeau’s career aspirations are not bound by the traditional limits of professional golf tours — he has plenty of options indeed. Which is why, as LIV’s bankruptcy rolled on and DeChambeau’s ex-coworkers released statements about their futures, DeChambeau remained quiet, before ending up somewhere nobody expected: Western Maine. (You can listen to a version of this story on the Drop Zone podcast below or here .) “ SUGARLOAF IS ONE OF THOSE HIDDEN-AWAY PLACES,” says Oscar Park, the course’s head professional. It’s 34 miles from the Canadian border. It’s 50 miles to the end of the Appalachian Trail. It’s two-and-a-half hours to Portland; Bangor is slightly closer, but offers fewer flights. “It’s remote,” Park says. “But also close enough to the real world that if you need a taste, you can get back to it real quick.” Sugarloaf doesn’t often get celebrity guests. Lucas Glover has family in Maine; he’s been there. So has Cooper Flagg , the First Hooper of Vacationland. But for five months of the year, it’s one of the best courses in the state (before it transforms to ski resort for the winter) and, Park says, they want the world to know. In the modern world of golf-course marketing, that means recruiting help from wherever you can get it; Park said his team felt like the course’s location, layout and conditioning made it worthy of extra attention. His assistant pros cast a wide net throughout the new-age content-creator world, and as a longshot dropped a line to DeChambeau’s team, too, on the off chance he might be interested. Sugarloaf didn’t get into specifics about exactly what it cost them to land DeChambeau, one of the biggest fish in the YouTube golf sea. Park said it “wasn’t cost prohibitive.” Sugarloaf had something he was looking for, after all — a new golf experience in a beautiful place, and a willingness to host him. And, Park added, the types of companies DeChambeau is looking for have bigger marketing budgets than Sugarloaf’s. Most touring pros don’t tick off bucket-list courses outside the bounds of their home courses, Tour stops and occasional nearby outings. But DeChambeau isn’t most touring pros. He ramped up his YouTube presence during his years on LIV Golf, making waves with a celebrity-based “Break 50” series. Recently, though, he seems to be zeroing in on one-off experiences, from playing golf in the redwoods of Northern California to a course in Banff, in the heart of the Canadian Rockies. It’s cool to see such a high-profile competitor lean into the sorts of trips everyday golfers dream of. It’s also rare, which makes it notable, particularly in the context of DeChambeau’s competitive future. But this is a guy who is openly searching for meaning, in different corners of the golf world and beyond. He opened up in a recent “Figuring Out” podcast interview , offering a glimpse into the questions he asked himself following his 2024 U.S. Open win: “I’ll never forget we had a nice party, we were all having fun and I go to bed. It’s tough to sleep, by the way — your endorphins and your adrenaline are still going. But you sleep for the five, six hours and you wake up and you look over and you’re like, ‘I won the U.S. Open’ and then right after, you say, ‘what do I do next?’ I’m in bed alone. I don’t have my family with me. I don’t have anybody around. And it’s a real moment of frailty. And it’s not easy because your entire life you’re told that’s what the goal is. The goal is to get to this trophy. And then you realize when you hit it, you go, ‘I gave up most of my life for this. I gave up 20 years of my life to do this and I did it. Well, now what do I do?’ And I don’t have anybody next to me. I don’t have somebody loving on me and giving me a kiss and a kid coming up on the bed and holding my hand and all that. Is that really what I want to do for my life? Is that what the legacy I want to leave too? And so it really transforms you and makes you realize what life is about. So, it’s a great thing. It’s also a humbling thing and it makes you feel lonely at first, but if you can get past that loneliness, you realize what life is truly about.” He didn’t get into specifics on what life is, in fact, about, but based on his actions we can surmise that at least part of what life is about is jetting off to Augusta on a whim — Augusta, Maine, that is — to catch the fall foliage. What was it like from the Sugarloaf side, getting word that DeChambeau was interested? “They were fantastic. I mean, they were very professional,” Park said. “They didn’t waste a lot of time. They didn’t have a ton of lists — no satin sheets and caviar for lunch or anything like that. I mean very much regular bunch of guys, you know, in the video, you know, Bryson’s eating a burger, you know, he basically pulled an all-nighter in getting there in itself…” I have to admit this was my favorite bit of the video and it came at the very beginning. I do not have the faintest idea what it’s like to fly private from Las Vegas to Augusta, Maine. I’m not sure anyone has ever done that before Bryson did a few weeks ago. But I am intimately familiar with the feeling of driving the roads of Northern New England at night, hoping to find something open — and settling for whatever you can get. I found Bryson’s gas-station stop more delightful than even his David Attenborough impression that would follow. I was curious, given everything going on in DeChambeau’s background, whether he’d made reference to his own competitive future. Parks said not really; he seemed immersed in his first-ever New England fall golf experience and was already wondering about coming back. It’s safe to say Sugarloaf would be happy to have him. Within a couple days the video had racked up more than 2 million views; a week later it’s over 3 million. That’s a lot of potential customers salivating over Carrabassett Valley views and fall foliage at a course they’d probably never heard of. “I feel like he did us a great justice, the golf course and the experience here,” Parks said of the final video. “I feel his words were impactful and spot on to what it feels like to play here, it being a special type of place, so I was delighted to see the finished product.” Parks said he got a kick out of just how ready DeChambeau was to geek out about his new surrounds; he got up close and personal with tree bark and leaves. Parks described him as a “good, clean and wholesome guy,” who doesn’t curse and was very present in his surroundings. It was an employee-and-member-guest day, which worked out as an extra perk for Sugarloaf’s VIPs, who got unexpected access to the two-time major champ. “Every single person who waited around for an autograph, he signed for them,” Parks said. “It was certainly an experience that no one’s going to forget anytime soon.” The most DeChambeau detail of all, which will sound familiar to anyone who’s covered his competitive career, was that, after his round, he couldn’t leave until he resolved a sticky swing thought. “He finished playing, he came in and talked and he was like, ‘I need to go hit balls. I need to go practice,'” Parks said. “And he signed some autographs, he went out for 45 minute

item.title: Cubs superstar Pete Crow-Armstrong gets 100% real on potentially winning MVP over Shohei Ohtani
item.description: Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images Cubs superstar Pete Crow-Armstrong gets 100% real on potentially winning MVP over Shohei Ohtani appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong is approaching Thursday’s National League MVP announcement with more on his mind than the possibility of beating Shohei Ohtani for the award. Crow-Armstrong joins the Los Angeles Dodgers superstar and Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang as the three finalists. MLB Network’s announcement show begins at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT. The recognition follows a season in which Crow-Armstrong combined power, speed and standout defense. Before learning the result, however, the Cubs star outfielder explained what he anticipates most about the evening. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Ross and Rizzo Unfiltered,” hosted by David Ross and Anthony Rizzo, shared a clip Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, capturing his perspective ahead of the reveal. “I’m flying in everybody that I feel has like played a direct part in my success. I get to have all of the people that I’m really grateful for in one place, and I think I’m most looking forward to that.” It would mean the WORLD for PCA to win the MVP surrounded by the people who made him the player he is today ❤️🏆 pic.twitter.com/rqYV9Eness — Ross and Rizzo Unfiltered (@RossAndRizzo) November 12, 2026 Crow-Armstrong also discussed his eagerness to turn his attention toward next season: “I don’t want to sound ungrateful. I think I’m mostly ready to just move past it. If I’m being honest, I love looking forward to the next season. It feels like Thursday might be my baseball New Year’s. I finally get to to move on.” The 24-year-old finished with 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases, becoming the first Cubs player to reach 40 homers and 40 steals in one season. He also ranked second in MLB with 48.8 weighted runs above average, behind AL MVP finalist Yordan Alvarez’s 62.7. Crow-Armstrong hit .280/.372/.570 with 107 RBIs and 119 runs in 162 games, adding a second consecutive Gold Glove. Thursday’s announcement will reveal whether he adds NL MVP honors, with voting completed before the postseason. Related: MLB rumors: Padres, Mariners, Cubs among teams linked to potential Jarren Duran trade with Red Sox Related: Unfortunate Ben Brown surgery revelation comes with hope for 2027 season

item.title: Ohio State’s only realistic playoff path runs through Indianapolis
item.description: Ohio State has never been ranked this low by the College Football Playoff committee. The Buckeyes fell from No. 12 to No. 20 in Tuesday’s second CFP rankings after losing to Oregon, the lowest ranking Ohio State has ever received since the committee started releasing rankings in 2014. It’s also the Buckeyes’ lowest spot in the AP and Coaches polls since 2014, the week after the home loss to Virginia Tech. So where does that leave Ohio State’s playoff hopes? I’ll be honest. I don’t think the Buckeyes are making the playoff this year. Their chances are a long shot, but there is one path, and it’s actually a little more realistic than some people might think. Why 9-3 probably isn’t enough The most obvious path is winning out. Ohio State has Northwestern, at Nebraska and Michigan left. Win all three, and the Buckeyes finish 9-3. The problem is that 9-3 doesn’t do much for this resume. None of Ohio State’s remaining opponents are ranked in the CFP top 25, so there’s no chance for a big win to impress the committee. The Buckeyes would still be sitting behind a long list of two loss teams, and their three losses, at Texas, at USC and at home against Oregon, came against teams ranked ahead of them. Look at the teams between Ohio State and the edge of the 12-team field. Kentucky, Texas Tech, Wake Forest, Houston, Iowa, Oregon, South Carolina, USC and Ole Miss. Most of them have fewer losses, and two of them beat Ohio State. Even if several of those teams lose, the Buckeyes would need a ton of chaos to climb from No. 20 into an at-large spot without a quality win left on the schedule. ESPN’s Football Power Index is more optimistic, giving Ohio State a 42.6% chance to make the playoff. I don’t buy it though. Unless something crazy happens, a 9-3 Ohio State is probably gonna be watching the playoff from home. The Big Ten title game is the only real path That’s why I think Ohio State’s best path, and honestly their only one, is to get to the Big Ten Championship Game and win it. Right now, the Big Ten standings don’t look great. UCLA is 9-0 and 6-0 in conference play, Indiana is 8-1 and 5-1, while USC and Oregon are both 4-2, just like Ohio State. The Buckeyes are also behind in the tiebreakers against USC and Oregon, since they lost to both. But this season has been anything but predictable, and things could get crazy. Here’s what Ohio State would need to make the Conference Championship Game: Win out — That gets the Buckeyes to 7-2 in conference play. Indiana loses at least once more — Ohio State beat Indiana in Bloomington, so if the Hoosiers fall to 7-2 in the Big Ten, the Buckeyes would own the head-to-head tiebreaker in a two-way tie. USC and Oregon both lose at least once more — Since both beat Ohio State, the Buckeyes would need to finish ahead of them outright. USC and Indiana play each other this week as well, so at least one of these three things will happen. UCLA wins out, or stumbles too — If UCLA keeps winning, they take one spot in Indianapolis

Right now, the Big Ten standings don’t look great. UCLA is 9-0 and 6-0 in conference play, Indiana is 8-1 and 5-1, while USC and Oregon are both 4-2, just like Ohio State. Here’s what Ohio State would need to make the Conference Championship Game: Win out — That gets the Buckeyes to 7-2 in conference play. Indiana loses at least once more — Ohio State beat Indiana in Bloomington, so if the Hoosiers fall to 7-2 in the Big Ten, the Buckeyes would own the head-to-head tiebreaker in a two-way tie. USC and Oregon both lose at least once more — Since both beat Ohio State, the Buckeyes would need to finish ahead of them outright. USC and Indiana play each other this week as well, so at least one of these three things will happen. UCLA wins out, or stumbles too — If UCLA keeps winning, they take one spot in Indianapolis. Ohio State would be competing for the other. That’s a lot of moving parts, and multi team ties could get complicated, but it isn’t impossible. USC has already lost to Wisconsin, Oregon has lost to UCLA and Illinois this season, and Indiana’s offense hasn’t looked the same since Ohio State held them to 15 points in October. One or two upsets could completely change the race. If Ohio State gets to Indianapolis and can win the final Big Ten Championship, they wouldn’t need the committee’s approval to enter the playoff. RIP to Big Ten Championship games 🥀 pic.twitter.com/S4Xrha1Pi9 — Woody (@woodyVSworld) November 9, 2026 What Ohio State can control The frustrating part is that Ohio State can’t control most of this. They need to win out, then hope Indiana, USC and Oregon all slip up. But the Buckeyes can at least give themselves a chance. That starts with fixing the defense, which has allowed 71 points over the last two games. It means Luke Fahey continuing to grow, Jeremiah Smith staying the focal point and the Buckeyes beating Michigan for a second straight year. Even if the playoff doesn’t happen, those things matter. There’s still plenty to play for. Smith is 31 yards from becoming the Big Ten’s all-time leading receiver . Beating Michigan would salvage a lot. A strong finish would build momentum heading into 2027, when Julian Sayin may potentially be back. But if you’re asking me whether Ohio State makes the playoff this year, my answer is unfortunately no. If it does happen though, it’ll almost certainly be because the Buckeyes found a way to Indianapolis and won the Big Ten. Anything less, and this season likely will end without a playoff berth.

item.title: ‘Get Rid of Them Both’ — Ex-NFL QB Urges Eagles To Make Decision on the Futures of Nick Sirianni, Jalen Hurts
item.description: Sep 28, 2025; Tampa, Florida, USA; Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni communicates with quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) during a timeout in the second quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. © Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Robert Griffin III thinks the Eagles need to decide what they want their future to look like. Seven straight losses have made the question increasingly uncomfortable. His answer ties Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts together. Philadelphia can commit to the coach-quarterback partnership or start over with both. Griffin even offered a holiday-relationship analogy for an organization trying to figure out whether the arrangement still works. Robert Griffin III Links Nick Sirianni’s Future to Jalen Hurts During an “Outta Pocket with RGIII” discussion, Griffin revisited his position on Sirianni after Philadelphia’s latest defeat extended its losing streak to seven games. Philadelphia’s latest defeat had extended its losing streak to seven games, prompting another look at that stance. “After seven straight losses for the Philadelphia Eagles, I think you stick with Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts, or you get rid of them both,” Griffin said . That full statement matters. Griffin left keeping both men firmly on the table. His argument was that ownership needs to make a clear decision about the partnership and the franchise’s direction. He also addressed Hurts’ health while explaining the timing of any potential move. “I’m not saying you trade him, trade Jalen Hurts at the trade deadline,” Griffin said. “He’s dealing with the blood clots right now. He might potentially be out for the year, so I’m not saying do that.” Hurts is on injured reserve and is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season after being diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. Griffin then placed the responsibility for the bigger decision with ownership. “But I am saying that as an owner of the team, you have to set the direction of the team,” he said. The discussion concerned Philadelphia’s longer-term plans, with Hurts’ absence complicating an already difficult evaluation. The quarterback has been recovering from blood clots, leaving Sirianni to navigate the season without him. Griffin has previously defended both Hurts and Sirianni while criticizing offensive coordinator Sean Mannion . His latest comments put the organizational decision under the microscope as losses continue to pile up. Joe Milton made his first start for the Eagles, and the offense again struggled to generate enough points. item.title: Nick Wright willing to wager $1 million to prove Clay Travis is a political grifter
item.description: Credit: FS1, Sport & State Nick Wright recently exposed Clay Travis for fabricating political beliefs to arouse his following, and he’s willing to bet $1 million on it. Wright joined Tim Miller on The Bulwark Daily podcast this week, where the FS1 host pulled back the curtain to reveal that Travis once admitted his beliefs and opinions are crafted for audience enrichment . According to Wright, Travis made the admission at a dinner about 11 years ago. Believing that’s worse than just having different political opinions, Wright told Travis he could not respect him, and claims to have left the dinner. Predictably, Travis fired back Wednesday night, attempting to dispute Wright by saying, “I guess this is what happens when you start voting Republican, people make up entire stories about you in their heads and share it with their far left wing friends.” Thursday morning, Wright had one final response to Travis, giving a detailed recount of the interaction 11 years ago and noting he has witnesses who will defend his side of the story before offering to bet $1 million to prove he’s telling the truth. I’m not going to go back and forth with you (it’s football season for God’s sake!), but I can’t believe you’re actually denying this interaction so I’ll jog your memory: August of 2016, during the Olympics, at the (now shuttered) Intercontinental hotel, a couple blocks from the Fox lot off Pico. We had just finished a night show that no longer exists where (among other things) we debated the Summer Olympics (it was a bad segment because we didn’t have rights to the footage, so we could only show still pictures of what we were talking about) & went to have a drink/meal with a colleague who was on the show with us. The exchange I discussed happened in the lobby bar, at a table with said colleague, and then after I said what I needed to say to to you I went outside and bummed a cigarette off a valet. We haven’t spoken in person since. You know as well as I do this is 100% true, and verifiable, by the colleague that was with us and/or our then bosses who contemporaneously heard the story. We actually also had the same agent at the time, and you and I both know he heard the story and could confirm it as well. So, I’ll pull a page out of your book; I’ll bet you $1,000,000 I’m telling the truth. I assume you’ll pretend you never saw this tweet & continue the grift. And that’s cool, but we both know what the facts are. Also, let this be a reminder that while you have found an amazing lane where you often are actually the smartest guy in the room, this ain’t that lane. So my advice would be to tread carefully. — nick wright (@getnickwright) November 12, 2026 “I’ll pull a page out of your book; I’ll bet you $1,000,000 I’m telling the truth,” Wright wrote. “Also, let this be a reminder that while you have found an amazing lane where you often are actually the smartest guy in the room, this ain’t that lane. item.content:encoded: Credit: FS1, Sport & State Nick Wright recently exposed Clay Travis for fabricating political beliefs to arouse his following, and he’s willing to bet $1 million on it. Wright joined Tim Miller on The Bulwark Daily podcast this week, where the FS1 host pulled back the curtain to reveal that Travis once admitted his beliefs and opinions are crafted for audience enrichment . According to Wright, Travis made the admission at a dinner about 11 years ago. Believing that’s worse than just having different political opinions, Wright told Travis he could not respect him, and claims to have left the dinner. Predictably, Travis fired back Wednesday night, attempting to dispute Wright by saying, “I guess this is what happens when you start voting Republican, people make up entire stories about you in their heads and share it with their far left wing friends.” Thursday morning, Wright had one final response to Travis, giving a detailed recount of the interaction 11 years ago and noting he has witnesses who will defend his side of the story before offering to bet $1 million to prove he’s telling the truth. I’m not going to go back and forth with you (it’s football season for God’s sake!), but I can’t believe you’re actually denying this interaction so I’ll jog your memory: August of 2016, during the Olympics, at the (now shuttered) Intercontinental hotel, a couple blocks from the Fox lot off Pico. We had just finished a night show that no longer exists where (among other things) we debated the Summer Olympics (it was a bad segment because we didn’t have rights to the footage, so we could only show still pictures of what we were talking about) & went to have a drink/meal with a colleague who was on the show with us. The exchange I discussed happened in the lobby bar, at a table with said colleague, and then after I said what I needed to say to to you I went outside and bummed a cigarette off a valet. We haven’t spoken in person since. You know as well as I do this is 100% true, and verifiable, by the colleague that was with us and/or our then bosses who contemporaneously heard the story. We actually also had the same agent at the time, and you and I both know he heard the story and could confirm it as well. So, I’ll pull a page out of your book; I’ll bet you $1,000,000 I’m telling the truth. I assume you’ll pretend you never saw this tweet & continue the grift. And that’s cool, but we both know what the facts are. Also, let this be a reminder that while you have found an amazing lane where you often are actually the smartest guy in the room, this ain’t that lane. So my advice would be to tread carefully. — nick wright (@getnickwright) November 12, 2026 “I’ll pull a page out of your book; I’ll bet you $1,000,000 I’m telling the truth,” Wright wrote. “Also, let this be a reminder that while you have found an amazing lane where you often are actually the smartest guy in the room, this ain’t that lane. So my advice would be to tread carefully.” Travis responded again by attempting to claim Wright just has a personal issue with him over Black Lives Matter. But in his response, which was surely meant to dunk on Wright, Travis claimed COVID broke him, leading him to vote for a Republican president for the first time in 2020. Travis then went on to say he would be willing to bet $1 million with Wright if a lie detector is involved so they can discuss transgender athletes, which has absolutely nothing to do with the bet Wright offered first. I can’t respond to @getnickwright’s post to me because he’s had me blocked on here since I said BLM was a total fraud and that LeBron faked the “hate crime” at his LA mansion. I was right, of course, about both of these things. I was a Democrat in 2015 — and 2016 — which he now says is the date of our dinner. He did not storm out of a dinner after telling me off. This is a very girly thing to brag about, but I’m pretty sure I would remember that because I would have found it funny. I don’t recall our dinner conversation from a decade ago, but I would presume it was similar to this private email I sent Nick that he posted on here back in 2017. You can read that if you wish. At the time I considered myself a radical moderate and felt alienated from the far left and far right. https://t.co/MKZnxUKEko Nick seems to spend a lot of time thinking about me since he’s now posted private emails and talked about private dinners from a decade+ ago. I’m flattered to be so memorable to him. I didn’t vote for a Republican for president until 2020. Covid radicalized me, as it did many people. As I’ve said and written for years, I didn’t leave the Democrat party, the Democrat party left me. If Nick wants to bet a million dollars on do I believe the things I say, I guess we can get a lie detector machine and fire it up. The first question can be, do you believe men pretending to be women should be allowed to play in women’s sports? I’m petty confident I will pass the test when I say hell no. Will you pass when you say yes, Nick? — Clay Travis (@ClayTravis) November 12, 2026 The bet Wright proposed was that his recall of Travis admitting he crafts political opinions for engagement 11 years ago was correct, and that Travis is now lying by claiming the conversation never happened. In the wake of their social media interaction, Wright has received strong support, with others sharing their own stories about when they learned Travis was a political grifter. the late, great ed aschoff told me a similar story in 2018. about how they were once cool but that he couldn’t fuck with travis after he revealed it was all an act. — Joel D. Anderson (@byjoelanderson) November 12, 2026 I’m honestly surprised that people are surprised by this. It’s one of the worst kept secrets in our business that dude has been lying about his political beliefs for a long time. I also have some receipts, but I’ll keep those to myself. Make no mistake, he isn’t the only one. There’s a lot of people in our business who are cosplaying for clicks and views. It’s one of the most shameful and dishonest things that one can do. I applaud Nick for keep it real. — Jemele Hill (@jemelehill) November 12, 2026 An old clip of Pardon My Take’s PFT Commenter claiming Travis once admitted to him that he saw an open market for a right-leaning sports host also resurfaced. PFT has the same basic story as @getnickwright: “Clay’s such a fraud. He literally told me back in like 2015, ‘There’s no market out there right now for right wing sports, so I’m just going to start becoming a right wing sports [guy]’ – he told me what he was going to do.” https://t.co/eAUR8xRkJ5 — Elijah Cone (@ElijahCone) November 12, 2026 Interestingly, PFT said the interaction with Travis occurred in 2015, which aligns with the 11-year-old conversation Wright recalls having with the Sport & State founder. While Travis says COVID “radicalized me,” he previously described the 2015 protests at the University of Missouri as his “ red pill, ” which again matches the timing of the conversations he allegedly had with PFT and Wright. Travis has been open about previously identifying as a Democrat. He’s been open about not voting for Trump in 2016, and only voting for his first Republican presidential candidate in 2020. He’s been open about seeing an available market for right-leaning sports content. Everyone knows his background is not that of a lifelong conservative. So, what part of Wright’s story is Travis really contesting? The post Nick Wright willing to wager $1 million to prove Clay Travis is a political grifter appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Rangers rumors: Texas linked to Japanese star, but there’s 1 big trade caveat
item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Rangers rumors: Texas linked to Japanese star, but there’s 1 big trade caveat appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Texas Rangers could face a difficult decision as they explore adding Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato . The club has reportedly shown serious interest in the 27-year-old, but its plans to maintain a flat payroll could complicate any pursuit . According to Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic , Texas has done extensive background work on Sato, though his potential price tag could exceed the team’s comfort level. The report also noted that the Rangers would almost certainly need to trade a high-salaried player to create enough financial flexibility. President of baseball operations Chris Young has indicated that the club intends to keep its 2027 payroll around its 2026 level of $190 million. Corey Seager could become a key trade candidate as the Rangers explore ways to bring Japanese talent to Texas. The club has reportedly shown a willingness to listen to offers for its star shortstop. Moving Seager could create payroll flexibility and help the Rangers pursue Teruaki Sato. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sato could give Texas an impact bat after an outstanding season with the Hanshin Tigers. The 27-year-old posted a .306 batting average with 39 home runs and 106 RBIs in 143 games. He also won the Central League Triple Crown. Hanshin has posted the slugger, opening a 45-day negotiating window for MLB teams. The Rangers are also pursuing Japanese pitching prospect Shoki Oda. The 18-year-old reportedly throws a 97 mph fastball and has drawn interest from the Yankees, Dodgers and Phillies. Texas may need to trade players for additional international bonus pool money to sign him. Landing both Japanese talents would address different needs for Texas. Teruaki Sato could strengthen the Rangers’ major league lineup, while Shoki Oda offers long-term potential for their pitching staff. However, Texas must first overcome its financial hurdles to sign both players. Related: Dodgers rumors: The star pitcher LA may trade if Tarik Skubal returns Related: Braves agree to $35 million contract with ex-Dodgers closer

item.title: ‘Tom Brady No Longer Cares About Boston’ — Columnist Highlights ‘Painfully Obvious’ Truth About Patriots Legend’s Actions
item.description: ‘Tom Brady No Longer Cares About Boston’ — Columnist Highlights ‘Painfully Obvious’ Truth About Patriots Legend’s Actions Tom Brady showed up to celebrate Rob Gronkowski, but Boston Globe columnist Ben Volin wanted him to give Patriots fans something to celebrate, too. Brady’s quiet presence at his former teammate’s Patriots Hall of Fame induction became the centerpiece of a sharp column questioning his relationship with New England. For Volin, attending the ceremony and waving to the crowd fell well short of the occasion. Ben Volin Takes Aim at Tom Brady’s Quiet Appearance Gronkowski’s induction took place on Saturday, Nov. 7, with Brady among those attending. The crowd greeted the former quarterback enthusiastically, according to Volin’s account, but never received the storytelling moment the columnist thought the celebration deserved. “It’s painfully obvious that Tom Brady no longer cares about Boston, New England, or Patriots fans,” Volin wrote in The Boston Globe . That is Volin’s interpretation of Brady’s behavior. His criticism centered on the gap between the welcome Brady received and how little he publicly contributed to the ceremony. “He waved to the crowd, but that was it. He sat on stage for an hour like a piece of furniture, not participating,” Volin wrote. “Brady showed up for Gronkowski, but did nothing for the fans.” BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator The furniture comparison leaves little doubt about how Volin viewed the appearance. In his telling, a few minutes at the microphone would have made an already meaningful day better. “He may call them ‘the greatest fans in the NFL,’ as he did at his Patriots Hall of Fame induction ceremony in 2024, and consider himself ‘the messenger here to tell the world just how amazing Patriots fans really are.’ His actions say he doesn’t give a darn,” Volin added. “Would it have been so hard to share five minutes of Gronk stories?” he asked. Volin also rejected the argument that Brady speaking would have pulled attention away from the honoree. He believed stories from Gronkowski’s longtime quarterback would have added to the celebration. In his telling, a few minutes at the microphone would have made an already meaningful day better. “He may call them ‘the greatest fans in the NFL,’ as he did at his Patriots Hall of Fame induction ceremony in 2024, and consider himself ‘the messenger here to tell the world just how amazing Patriots fans really are.’ His actions say he doesn’t give a darn,” Volin added. “Would it have been so hard to share five minutes of Gronk stories?” he asked. Volin also rejected the argument that Brady speaking would have pulled attention away from the honoree. He believed stories from Gronkowski’s longtime quarterback would have added to the celebration. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer It is an understandable expectation for that particular pairing. Fans spent years watching their connection on the field. A ceremony honoring Gronkowski provided a natural setting to hear about moments that never made it to the air. Still, Brady’s attendance itself was a gesture of support. How much more he owed the audience is the disagreement driving Volin’s column. Brady’s Foxborough Return Reopens an Emotional Debate The ceremony was part of a larger reunion weekend. Brady returned to Gillette Stadium as Fox’s lead NFL analyst for Sunday’s game against Green Bay, while the Patriots also honored their Super Bowl LI championship team. The current team had a difficult afternoon. New England lost 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three first-half interceptions. Despite that performance, Maye ranks No. 4 through Week 9 with a PFN QB Impact Score of 83.7 . Brady was there to evaluate that team from the booth, while the weekend’s celebrations kept pulling the conversation back toward his own era. Volin’s criticism extended beyond one appearance. He contrasted Brady’s public praise for Patriots supporters with what he considers an insufficient connection to the region after spending 20 seasons there. The columnist also questioned Brady’s broader community legacy, while acknowledging that his work with Best Buddies “raised tens of millions of dollars.” That acknowledgment complicates any blanket suggestion that Brady left nothing behind off the field. Ultimately, Volin’s strongest complaint was a small, specific one. He wanted Brady to pick up a microphone and tell a few stories about Gronkowski. Whether that silence supports his much larger conclusion is open to debate. Brady attended a celebration for an old teammate. Volin saw an opportunity to reconnect with an entire fan base and believes Brady let it pass. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: AFCONQ: Why I didn’t invite Maduka Okoye – Chelle
item.description: Super Eagles head coach Eric Chelle has explained his decision to leave goalkeeper Maduka Okoye out of Nigeria’s squad for their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches. Chelle, who is preparing the Super Eagles for their double-header against Tanzania, said his selection decisions were based on considerations both on and off the pitch. The Franco-Malian tactician insisted that the national team was not obligated to any particular player, stressing that his choices were guided by his assessment of what was best for the squad. “The national team is not close to him or anyone. I made my choice and when I made my choice I made it around the pitch and outside it,” Chelle said. Okoye, who plays for Italian club Udinese, has been absent from recent Super Eagles selections, with Stanley Nwabali, Francis Uzoho and Arthur Okonkwo among the goalkeepers considered by the coach. Chelle’s latest comments underline his position that selection for the national team is based on his technical and other considerations rather than a player’s reputation or status. The Super Eagles are seeking to strengthen their position in the AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign as they prepare to face Tanzania in two crucial Group L encounters. Vanguard News The post AFCONQ: Why I didn’t invite Maduka Okoye – Chelle appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 12, 2014: European Philae probe lands on Comet 67P, bounced twice and then got lost for nearly 2 years
item.description: null On Nov. 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P . To say it was a bumpy landing would be an understatement. The European Space Agency's Philae lander separated from an orbiter called Rosetta ahead of its historic landing in 2014. It was supposed to use harpoons to secure itself on to the surface of Comet 67P, but the harpoons never fired. When it touched down, it immediately bounced back up into space . The first bounce brought Philae half a mile above the comet's surface before gravity brought it back down. Philae was missing for almost two years before scientists found it . Images from Rosetta showed Philae stuck in a dark crevice on top of the rubber duck-shaped comet. The European Space Agency's Rosetta spacecraft captured these photos of the Philae lander descending toward, and then bouncing off, the surface of Comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko during its historic touchdown on Nov. 12, 2014. (Image credit: ESA/Rosetta/MPS for OSIRIS Team MPS/UPD/LAM/IAA/SSO/INTA/UPM/DASP/IDA) Why it mattered The European Space Agency 's Rosetta and Philae expedition was a first-of-its-kind mission, an endeavour to not just rendezvous with a comet and watch it change over time as it approached the sun (that was Rosetta's job), but also to soft-land a probe on its icy and rocky surface to see what a comet is truly made of. The Rosetta and Philae mission succeeded on both counts, but Philae's historic landing was marred by its turbulent touchdown. Philae actually landed three different times on Comet 67/P , all because the harpoons designed to secure it in place didn't fire as planned. After the first landing, Philae bounced up and drifted around the comet for two hours, making another bounce before Rosetta's cameras lost track of it. Scientists figured it was stuck in a shady spot where sunlight couldn't reach its solar panels. Because it was solar-powered, Philae needed to be facing the sun properly to generate enough power for sustained operation on the comet's surface. Still, Philae did have some power stored in batteries, which lasted for more than two days on the surface. That allowed Philae to perform some science with its 10 instruments in the time it had on Comet 67/P. Most notably, Philae found organic molecules that had never been detected on a comet before. The Rosetta orbiter continued to orbit Comet 67P until September 2016, and it was in that month -- just weeks before Rosetta itself landed on the comet on Sept. 30, 2016 -- that the spacecraft rediscovered the Philae lander lying on its side in a rocky crevice. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: I Am Artemis Katie Spicer
item.description: 4 Min Read I Am Artemis Katie Spicer For Katie Spicer, embracing opportunity and challenge has led to giant leaps during her time at NASA. Now as the NASA lander integration lead for Blue Origin’s Blue Moon Mark 2 lander, one of the commercially provided human landing systems for NASA’s Artemis program, Spicer will have her handprint on history. NASA’s Katie Spicer stands in front of the crew cabin prototype for Blue Origin’s Blue Moon Mark 2 lunar lander. The lander is one of two commercial human landing systems that will help safely ferry astronauts from lunar orbit to the Moon’s surface and back for the agency’s crewed Artemis missions in 2028. NASA/Bill Strafford Spicer works in the Flight Operations Directorate at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston, where she evaluates and monitors design and development of Blue Origin’s lander. The design of the Blue Moon lander is rapidly evolving as Blue Origin continues to develop a streamlined lander test article for the agency’s Artemis III rendezvous and docking mission in low Earth orbit as well as a fully functional lander for a crewed lunar landing in 2028. Spicer works closely with her NASA and Blue Origin counterparts to ensure the design of the Blue Moon lander can support the overall Artemis mission objectives. “I look at the design of everything Artemis crews will touch, work with, or interface with to ensure systems will function the way crews will need them to,” Spicer said. “In some cases, the design might meet requirements, but I delve deeper into details. How easy will it be for crew to grab handles or handrails? Can they operate push-button displays in microgravity? Are the hygiene systems as user-friendly as possible in the limited space that’s available in the spacecraft? And, are there proper procedures and training to ensure the crew can safely and effectively use the systems? Evaluating all these operational details with crew perspective is part of my job.” Spicer has spent her career looking at the small details in the big picture. After earning a bachelor’s degree in microbiology from the Pennsylvania State University in State College, Spicer spent several years working as a full-time homemaker and raising three children. She got her start at NASA working part-time in the historic Life Sciences Laboratory , performing duties such as washing dishes, cleaning lab equipment, and running tests for scientists. “I went from tidying up and keeping my home running to maintaining the historic lab where the Apollo crews were quarantined when they came back from the Moon and the Moon rock samples were stored,” Spicer said. From there, Spicer began working with science payloads on the space station. item.dc:creator: Lee Mohon
item.content:encoded: 4 Min Read I Am Artemis Katie Spicer For Katie Spicer, embracing opportunity and challenge has led to giant leaps during her time at NASA. Now as the NASA lander integration lead for Blue Origin’s Blue Moon Mark 2 lander, one of the commercially provided human landing systems for NASA’s Artemis program, Spicer will have her handprint on history. NASA’s Katie Spicer stands in front of the crew cabin prototype for Blue Origin’s Blue Moon Mark 2 lunar lander. The lander is one of two commercial human landing systems that will help safely ferry astronauts from lunar orbit to the Moon’s surface and back for the agency’s crewed Artemis missions in 2028. NASA/Bill Strafford Spicer works in the Flight Operations Directorate at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston, where she evaluates and monitors design and development of Blue Origin’s lander. The design of the Blue Moon lander is rapidly evolving as Blue Origin continues to develop a streamlined lander test article for the agency’s Artemis III rendezvous and docking mission in low Earth orbit as well as a fully functional lander for a crewed lunar landing in 2028. Spicer works closely with her NASA and Blue Origin counterparts to ensure the design of the Blue Moon lander can support the overall Artemis mission objectives. “I look at the design of everything Artemis crews will touch, work with, or interface with to ensure systems will function the way crews will need them to,” Spicer said. “In some cases, the design might meet requirements, but I delve deeper into details. How easy will it be for crew to grab handles or handrails? Can they operate push-button displays in microgravity? Are the hygiene systems as user-friendly as possible in the limited space that’s available in the spacecraft? And, are there proper procedures and training to ensure the crew can safely and effectively use the systems? Evaluating all these operational details with crew perspective is part of my job.” Spicer has spent her career looking at the small details in the big picture. After earning a bachelor’s degree in microbiology from the Pennsylvania State University in State College, Spicer spent several years working as a full-time homemaker and raising three children. She got her start at NASA working part-time in the historic Life Sciences Laboratory , performing duties such as washing dishes, cleaning lab equipment, and running tests for scientists. “I went from tidying up and keeping my home running to maintaining the historic lab where the Apollo crews were quarantined when they came back from the Moon and the Moon rock samples were stored,” Spicer said. From there, Spicer began working with science payloads on the space station. She helped operate the Human Research Facility racks in the International Space Station National Laboratory and worked with scientists and crew to ensure in-flight processes and protocols were completed. It was there that Spicer found a love for the fast-paced dynamic of real-time space operations. Spicer became a flight controller at NASA Johnson’s Mission Control Center in 2018. The learning curve to become a flight controller was steep, but it did not deter her. Spicer studied and trained for five years to earn the ultimate instructor and flight controller certifications. “Unlike most people I work with, I don’t have an engineering degree,” Spicer said. “On my own, I studied engineering principles. I passed boards and certification tests. I learned to speak ‘engineer!’” Spicer spent five years as an Operations and Support Officer in the space station’s flight control room in Mission Control, also known as the “front room” to spaceflight. Now, when she looks at the Moon in the night sky, Spicer says she’s humbled and honored to be part of the team that’s sending astronauts back to the lunar surface. “I’m reminded of the great responsibility that NASA has in this endeavor, of the legacy of the courageous Apollo crews who went before, and inspiring the next generation of space explorers to keep going and reaching for the stars!” she said. As part of a Golden Age of innovation and exploration, NASA will send Artemis astronauts on increasingly difficult missions near the lunar South Pole to explore more of the Moon than ever before. In addition to providing economic benefits and advancing scientific discovery through its Moon missions, NASA will establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface and build on the agency’s foundation for the first crewed mission to Mars. item.title: AFCON 2027Q: Guinea-Bissau drop points, hand Super Eagles chance to close gap
item.description: Nigeria’s Super Eagles have received a boost in their quest to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after Guinea-Bissau were held to a 1-1 draw by Madagascar in their Group L encounter on Thursday. The result offers Nigeria an opportunity to reduce the gap at the top of the group following Guinea-Bissau’s impressive start to the qualifying campaign. The Djurtus had taken control of Group L after recording a 3-0 victory over the Super Eagles in their Matchday Two encounter last month. However, they were unable to maintain their winning run against Madagascar, needing a late goal to salvage a point. Warren Caddy gave Madagascar the lead a minute before the hour mark, putting Guinea-Bissau under pressure. But Galatasaray forward Renato Nhaga came to the visitors’ rescue, scoring six minutes from time to secure a 1-1 draw. The result leaves Guinea-Bissau top of Group L with seven points from three matches, while Madagascar sit third with two points. Nigeria can take advantage of the dropped points when they host Tanzania’s Taifa Stars in Uyo on Friday. A victory would strengthen the Super Eagles’ position in the group and provide a much-needed boost to their qualification hopes after their heavy defeat to Guinea-Bissau. The encounter is therefore crucial for Nigeria as they seek to get their AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign back on track. item.title: Lego marketplace BrickLink in pieces after 'unusual activity' takes it offline for almost a week
item.description: Lego-owned marketplace BrickLink has been offline for almost a week after identifying "unusual activity on the platform," leaving fans unable to buy and sell spare bricks and minifigures. The company initially described the outage as "necessary work" and said the site would return on November 9. That deadline has come and gone. Visiting BrickLink's domain automatically serves the platform's maintenance page, which was last updated on November 11. "We took BrickLink offline after identifying unusual activity on the platform," the website states. "Our immediate priority was to secure the site, protect our members and ensure the integrity of BrickLink. "Before bringing the site back online, we need to fully understand what has happened. That means containing the issue, investigating how it happened and checking for related issues. "This work is still ongoing and we appreciate your patience while we work to get things back online as soon as possible." The references to security, containment, and investigation suggest something beyond routine maintenance, although BrickLink has not confirmed whether it suffered a cyberattack. The Register asked Lego for more information, but it did not immediately respond. Some adult fans of Lego (AFOL) have criticized the lack of information since the outage began on Friday, November 6. "Imagine how much better this would have been received if they were transparent from day one instead of pretending they have control over something they clearly don't," said one disgruntled Legohead via Reddit. "They don't even need to say what went wrong," said another. "Just an email acknowledging the issue would be appropriate. The entire site is down, and has been for days. That warrants more than a splash page." BrickLink was launched by Dan Jezek in June 2000 as an independent marketplace for enthusiasts to buy and sell Lego sets and individual pieces, including discontinued parts and rare minifigures. The Lego Group acquired BrickLink and Sohobricks from investment outfit NXMH in 2019 for an undisclosed sum. NXMH had bought BrickLink in 2013 and also owned Sohobricks, a South Korean manufacturer of unofficial but Lego-compatible bricks. Lego shuttered Sohobricks in 2020. At the time of Lego's acquisition, BrickLink had more than 10,000 storefronts on its marketplace selling Lego sets, parts, and minifigures. The AFOL community was initially concerned about Big Brick's intention with the acquisition, fearing that it would lead to high prices closer to those on Lego's own Pick a Brick parts-ordering service. For now, buyers and sellers would probably settle for a marketplace that's actually online. ®

item.title: Jensen Huang's self-sabotage sends Nvidia into a midlife crisis
item.description: Nvidia CEO and founder Jensen Huang has been ousted after nearly two weeks of controversy that, at times, felt more like a soap opera than reality: a wealthy businessman, reported affairs, and an alleged Chinese spy and GPU smuggler. For Nvidia’s board, it seems there was no question Huang had to go. The man behind what was recently the most valuable company in the world proved too big a liability to retain in any capacity. He was too toxic even for a demotion from CEO to chairman, a vantage point that would have retained Huang as the face of the company even if he could no longer be trusted to run it. Replacing him won’t be so easy. Nvidia now faces an identity crisis. Huang, who has led the company for more than three decades, has no clear successor. The GPU slinger has no shortage of brilliant engineers, but executives capable of wrangling one of the biggest and most influential brands in the world, not so much. Ian Buck, father of CUDA and Nvidia’s VP of hyperscale and HPC is currently favored by many to be Huang’s successor. Buck has taken on a more public role within Nvidia in recent years headlining keynotes at events like Supercomputing and the AI Infra Summit. CFO Colette Kress, a bean counter who’s kept Jensen’s ambitions grounded for more than a decade, now takes the reins as interim CEO while the board searches for its next figurehead. And while Kress fights to contain the chaos, others will no doubt capitalize on Huang’s controversial choice of consorts to advance their own agendas. A marred reputation One need only ask a few inconvenient questions to cast doubt on Nvidia’s loyalties. How deep does China’s influence in Nvidia go? Can Nvidia’s hardware still be trusted? You get the idea. It certainly wouldn’t be the first time Nvidia’s and, by extension, Huang’s loyalties have been called into question. In late 2023, Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman blasted rival Nvidia for supplying GPUs to China in spite of US export controls, calling the behavior “ un-American ” and likening the graphics titan to an AI arms dealer. Nvidia has also faced criticism from US government officials, including former commerce secretary Gina Raimondo, for failing to take a hint and trying instead to limbo under US export controls in order to continue selling chips to the Middle Kingdom. After the Trump administration's short lived blockade of H20 sales early last year cost the company some $10.5 billion, Huang spent much of the 2025 lobbying the Trump administration to reverse export bans on the sales of older Hopper generation GPUs to China, an endeavor which ultimately proved successful . One could make the case that Huang’s ongoing efforts to sell Nvidia’s chips to China were financially motivated. But that argument is undermined by Huang admitting to having an extramarital affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang (no relation), a woman that US intelligence has accused of moonlighting as a Chinese spy and helping to smuggle GPUs into the country. item.dc:creator: Tobias Mann
item.content:encoded: Nvidia CEO and founder Jensen Huang has been ousted after nearly two weeks of controversy that, at times, felt more like a soap opera than reality: a wealthy businessman, reported affairs, and an alleged Chinese spy and GPU smuggler. For Nvidia’s board, it seems there was no question Huang had to go. The man behind what was recently the most valuable company in the world proved too big a liability to retain in any capacity. He was too toxic even for a demotion from CEO to chairman, a vantage point that would have retained Huang as the face of the company even if he could no longer be trusted to run it. Replacing him won’t be so easy. Nvidia now faces an identity crisis. Huang, who has led the company for more than three decades, has no clear successor. The GPU slinger has no shortage of brilliant engineers, but executives capable of wrangling one of the biggest and most influential brands in the world, not so much. Ian Buck, father of CUDA and Nvidia’s VP of hyperscale and HPC is currently favored by many to be Huang’s successor. Buck has taken on a more public role within Nvidia in recent years headlining keynotes at events like Supercomputing and the AI Infra Summit. CFO Colette Kress, a bean counter who’s kept Jensen’s ambitions grounded for more than a decade, now takes the reins as interim CEO while the board searches for its next figurehead. And while Kress fights to contain the chaos, others will no doubt capitalize on Huang’s controversial choice of consorts to advance their own agendas. A marred reputation One need only ask a few inconvenient questions to cast doubt on Nvidia’s loyalties. How deep does China’s influence in Nvidia go? Can Nvidia’s hardware still be trusted? You get the idea. It certainly wouldn’t be the first time Nvidia’s and, by extension, Huang’s loyalties have been called into question. In late 2023, Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman blasted rival Nvidia for supplying GPUs to China in spite of US export controls, calling the behavior “ un-American ” and likening the graphics titan to an AI arms dealer. Nvidia has also faced criticism from US government officials, including former commerce secretary Gina Raimondo, for failing to take a hint and trying instead to limbo under US export controls in order to continue selling chips to the Middle Kingdom. After the Trump administration's short lived blockade of H20 sales early last year cost the company some $10.5 billion, Huang spent much of the 2025 lobbying the Trump administration to reverse export bans on the sales of older Hopper generation GPUs to China, an endeavor which ultimately proved successful . One could make the case that Huang’s ongoing efforts to sell Nvidia’s chips to China were financially motivated. But that argument is undermined by Huang admitting to having an extramarital affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang (no relation), a woman that US intelligence has accused of moonlighting as a Chinese spy and helping to smuggle GPUs into the country. The consequences of controversy When technology and politics collide, the appearance of impropriety is often more damning than the impropriety itself. Uncle Sam has forced Chinese companies out of the United States for the mere possibility that they could be coerced into planting back doors in critical infrastructure. Just ask Huawei whether the truth counts for anything once Washington has decided that you’re a national security threat. Huang’s affairs may not just cost him his job, but could cost Nvidia key government contracts and make the company’s hardware less attractive, particularly in highly-regulated and notoriously risk-averse industries. Rival chipmakers will no doubt capitalize on Nvidia’s bad optics if Huang’s departure doesn’t pop the AI financing merry-go-round bubble first – Nvidia's stock lost about 25% of its value in the few days after news about Huang started breaking, only recovering slightly after his ouster. Regardless, with Nvidia’s reputation marred and its future shrouded in uncertainty, once loyal customers may be more willing to explore alternative providers. There are certainly plenty to choose from. Amid a surge in custom AI chips from the likes of Broadcom, Marvel, and others, Nvidia’s main advantage wasn’t so much technological as it was simply considered a safe bet. AMD is the most obvious winner here. As we reported earlier this year , the House of Zen’s GPU tech has already surpassed Nvidia’s, at least on paper. What’s more, the company has a long and unblemished relationship serving the US government. AMD’s chips now power two of the Department of Energy’s three largest and most sensitive supercomputers. Meanwhile, hyperscalers with sufficient cashflow – think Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta – may seek to insulate themselves from Huang’s fallout by investing more heavily in homegrown silicon and offering it to customers. Then there's the threat from the man himself. Huang's ambitions and influence are such that he's unlikely to fade into obscurity. He may disappear from the spotlight while things blow over, but it’s a pretty sure bet that he’ll pop up at a new company eventually, and will still have enough sway to poach some of Nvidia’s top engineers. ®

item.title: Arsenal dig deep to earn WCL draw in face of Barcelona dominance
item.description: Arsenal continue to be a sharp thorn in the side of the European champions, Barcelona, digging deep to hold on to a draw here. Frida Maanum put the Gunners ahead despite a hugely dominant performance from Barcelona, but Caroline Graham Hansen’s equaliser ensured the spoils would be shared. The last time these two teams met, Arsenal were lifting aloft the Champions League trophy at Barcelona’s expense after the most perfect of defensive performances and a Stina Blackstenius goal in Lisbon in 2025. It was a far less perfect defensive performance this time, but Arsenal showed guts against the team that retook their crown last season and showed they can play ugly when needed. Continue reading...

item.title: AI confirms a long-suspected limit on quantum computers’ advantages

item.title: SpaceX's Starship megarocket will launch to orbit on Nov. 13. Will you be able to spot it in the night sky?
item.description: null SpaceX's Starship megarocket is slated to launch on its ambitious 15th flight test as soon as this Friday (Nov. 13). Will you be able to spot its leviathan upper stage, known as Ship, or its Starlink satellite passengers as they circle Earth during the historic orbital jaunt? Flight 15's 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT) on Nov. 13 . Starship will fly from SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas, where it will be 4:45 p.m. at the opening of the window — about an hour before sunset. The launch could therefore be especially dramatic for folks in the area. "As it launches towards the southeast, and it will be daylight, then the prospects for viewing from the U.S. are going to be in Texas and the states along the Gulf of Mexico," Robert Massey, deputy executive director at the Royal Astronomical Society, told Space.com. "They could see the exhaust plume (the ' jellyfish ') with the sky darker for observers further east." If all goes to plan, Starship's Super Heavy booster will propel the Ship upper stage through the densest part of Earth's atmosphere before returning to Starbase for a powered landing and capture via the "chopstick" arms of the "Mechazilla" tower system . Ship, meanwhile, will go on to orbit Earth approximately 14 times over the following 22 hours, during which time it will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before returning to Starbase for its own ambitious catch attempt. When should I look for Starship and its Starlink train? Satellite visibility in the night sky depends on a cocktail of factors, from the size of the spacecraft to its reflectivity, orbital inclination and position relative to the Earth and sun. Ship is big — about 171 feet (52 meters) tall — so it will be a viable target for skywatchers, experts say. "It certainly will be visible in twilight hours. It should be very bright, considerably brighter than the Starlink satellites due to its size," professor James Osborn of Durham University told Space.com. "Where and when is a bit more tricky." Starship Flight 14 rises away from its launch tower during the September 2026 test flight from Boca Chica, Texas. (Image credit: Photo by Brandon Bell/Getty Images) Ship and its Starlink satellites may be seen in the 90 minutes directly after sunset on Nov. 13 and before sunrise on Nov. 14, as the probes catch the sunlight on either side of Earth's colossal shadow as they drift through the twilight sky. The spacecraft will initially appear as a string of bright, evenly spaced lights, with Ship most likely appearing significantly brighter than the Starlink satellites. However, Osborn noted that the lack of publicly available data makes it challenging to forecast exactly when the spacecraft will appear. "During its 14 orbits over 22 hours, the spacecraft is between inclinations of 30.5 [degrees] N and S of the equator," explained Massey. item.dc:creator: Anthony Wood
item.content:encoded: null SpaceX's Starship megarocket is slated to launch on its ambitious 15th flight test as soon as this Friday (Nov. 13). Will you be able to spot its leviathan upper stage, known as Ship, or its Starlink satellite passengers as they circle Earth during the historic orbital jaunt? Flight 15's 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT) on Nov. 13 . Starship will fly from SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas, where it will be 4:45 p.m. at the opening of the window — about an hour before sunset. The launch could therefore be especially dramatic for folks in the area. "As it launches towards the southeast, and it will be daylight, then the prospects for viewing from the U.S. are going to be in Texas and the states along the Gulf of Mexico," Robert Massey, deputy executive director at the Royal Astronomical Society, told Space.com. "They could see the exhaust plume (the ' jellyfish ') with the sky darker for observers further east." If all goes to plan, Starship's Super Heavy booster will propel the Ship upper stage through the densest part of Earth's atmosphere before returning to Starbase for a powered landing and capture via the "chopstick" arms of the "Mechazilla" tower system . Ship, meanwhile, will go on to orbit Earth approximately 14 times over the following 22 hours, during which time it will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before returning to Starbase for its own ambitious catch attempt. When should I look for Starship and its Starlink train? Satellite visibility in the night sky depends on a cocktail of factors, from the size of the spacecraft to its reflectivity, orbital inclination and position relative to the Earth and sun. Ship is big — about 171 feet (52 meters) tall — so it will be a viable target for skywatchers, experts say. "It certainly will be visible in twilight hours. It should be very bright, considerably brighter than the Starlink satellites due to its size," professor James Osborn of Durham University told Space.com. "Where and when is a bit more tricky." Starship Flight 14 rises away from its launch tower during the September 2026 test flight from Boca Chica, Texas. (Image credit: Photo by Brandon Bell/Getty Images) Ship and its Starlink satellites may be seen in the 90 minutes directly after sunset on Nov. 13 and before sunrise on Nov. 14, as the probes catch the sunlight on either side of Earth's colossal shadow as they drift through the twilight sky. The spacecraft will initially appear as a string of bright, evenly spaced lights, with Ship most likely appearing significantly brighter than the Starlink satellites. However, Osborn noted that the lack of publicly available data makes it challenging to forecast exactly when the spacecraft will appear. "During its 14 orbits over 22 hours, the spacecraft is between inclinations of 30.5 [degrees] N and S of the equator," explained Massey. "So it will be best viewed between those latitudes, and then lower in the sky up to latitudes of 40 N and 40 S. That's pretty much the whole of the contiguous U.S." Space.com skywatching columnist and veteran meteorologist Joe Rao shared further details on what stargazers may see with the naked eye as Ship drifts silently through the autumn sky. Starlink satellites form a trail of star-like points in the night sky soon after deployment in 2023. (Image credit: Photo by Arda Kucukkaya/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images) "When it passes overhead, it will look like a bright, fast-moving star crossing the sky — similar to the International Space Station , but potentially even brighter depending on its orientation," explained Rao. "The Starlink V3 satellites are much smaller, so not as bright, perhaps ranging anywhere from 2nd to 4th magnitude, depending on the angle of illumination with reflected light from the sun ." Magnitude is the scale used by astronomers to measure the brightness of objects in the night sky. The lower the magnitude, the brighter the object! The unaided eye can make out objects with a magnitude of around +6.5 under ideal dark sky conditions, while the planet Venus currently shines at magnitude -4.41. The Starlink train will likely fall further behind Starship as the 22-hour mission progresses, while the train itself will become more elongated, according to Rao. "For locations where it will make a high arc across the sky, the Starship should be visible for at least a few minutes, although because it is orbiting at a lower altitude (170 miles/275 km) compared to the ISS, it probably will appear to move somewhat faster. " How can I track Starship after launch? There are multiple handy resources that should allow you to track Ship and the newly deployed batch of V3 Starlink satellites following their scheduled launch on Nov. 13, including the websites Heavens-Above , Star Dash , Orbital Radar and Find Starlink . Be sure to keep an eye on our Starship Flight 15 live blog for all the latest news along with our launch timings article containing details on how to watch SpaceX's potentially historic orbital launch attempt. Editor's Note: If you capture a photo of Starship and want to share it with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: Ars Live: What drone attacks on data centers mean for modern life in the cloud
item.description: Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life. To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled "Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech" on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki , a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts. Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans. Read full article Comments

item.title: 2027: Trust me, I won’t fail you, INEC chair assures Nigerians
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has asked Nigerians to trust him to deliver a free, fair, credible and inclusive election next year, promising to not fail them This was as he said the commission is yet to recover from the trust deficit created by the technical glitches associated with the 2023 general election, and vowed that inaccurate polling unit results will not reach the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV in 2027. Amupitan spoke on Thursday at Chatham House, London, at a dialogue held with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) on the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” His Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said the INEC chairman noted that the controversies over the 2023 presidential election badly dented public confidence in the commission. “First, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC—damage so large that the Commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said. He said the commission’s audit after 2023 traced the worst result management failures to collation centres, not polling units. “In 2023, there were instances of inaccurate results or results with over-voting being uploaded onto IReV. We have now devised a technical safeguard: if a result is not accurate at the polling unit, it will not go to IReV at all. The moment a result appears on IReV, citizens can trust what they see. By eliminating inconsistencies at the source, collation will become a transparent formality”, he stated. The INEC chairman announced that the commission would hold a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28, 2026. “On the 28th of this month, we will conduct a mock accreditation and voting exercise across all states of the federation to simulate the presidential election and verify that we have gotten both accreditation and electronic result transmission right,” he said. Asked why Nigerians should trust his leadership, Amupitan who assumed office in October 2025, pointed to the off-cycle elections he had conducted. “Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said. He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections.
