item.title: The replicants are running the city in thrilling final trailer for ‘Blade Runner 2099’ (video)
item.description: null One of the most anticipated fall TV series, " Blade Runner 2099 , " recently dropped its final neon-tinted trailer, and now we’ve finally got a handle on the plot dynamics of this dystopian thriller set in the cyberpunk world of Ridley Scott's original. Prime Video's bold and brooding 8-episode series lands Nov. 25 as a tangential sequel to Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049," unfolding some 50 years after the 2017 feature film. Now the artificial inmates are running the asylum when violent replicant uprisings flip the script, causing humanity to become second-class citizens. "In Los Angeles 2099, Cora (Hunter Schafer) lived her entire life on the run, a chameleon forced to adopt numerous identities," states Prime Video's synopsis. "To secure a stable future for her brother, she assumes one final identity and is forced to partner with Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a Blade Runner who’s confronting the end of her life. The two are pulled into a widening conspiracy that poses an existential threat to a city that’s fighting to be reborn." This engrossing final trailer reveals more of the detailed noir world and Cora's plight to blend into society as a Blade Runner who links up with Olwen, an aging replicant exterminator, for an uneasy partnership. Here, a tense scene plays out in this preview as Cora undergoes an intense police station screening while being used as a resistance pawn to help take back the city from usurping androids. But another deep mystery lies hidden in plain sight! "You have to see the lie that is in front of you," warns Yeoh's dying synthetic cop. Will "Blade Runner 2099" usher in a new era for the sci-fi franchise? (Image credit: Prime Video) " Blade Runner 2099 " sports a spirited cast that includes Dimitri Abold ("The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes") and Lewis Gribben ("Somewhere Boy”) in collaboration with Katelyn Rose Downey ("The Nun II"), Daniel Rigby ('Renegade Nell"), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow"), Amy Lennox ("Only Child"), Sheila Atim ("The Woman King") and Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon”). Delivered by creator and showrunner Silka Louisa ("Shining Girls"), and executive produced by Silka Louisa and Ridley Scott’s Scott Free Productions, "Blade Runner 2099" lands on Prime Video beginning Nov. 25, 2026 .

item.title: Pan-African Vibes, Epic Bar Battles, and More! Lagos Cocktail Week 2026 was an Unforgettable Experience
item.description: The 12th edition of Africa’s biggest cocktail celebration, Lagos Cocktail Week (LCW), brought its 2026 theme, “Africa Pours into Lagos,” to life in spectacular fashion, delivering an exciting fusion of Pan-African creativity, cross-border collaborations, spirited competitions, and immersive experiences that celebrated the continent’s vibrant and evolving cocktail culture. Held from October 16 to 23, 2026, the week-long festival took cocktail culture beyond borders, bringing together some of the most exciting talents and bar communities from Lagos, Accra, and Abidjan. At the heart of this year’s celebration was a powerful message: Africa’s cocktail industry thrives when creativity, culture, and expertise flow freely across borders. The celebrations took off on Sunday, October 18, as the Italian Trade Agency brought a touch of Italian sophistication to the festival with the Italian Cocktail Experience, an exclusive, invitation-only masterclass and Aperitivo Italiano held at Mr Panther, Victoria Island. The experience offered guests an opportunity to explore the artistry and traditions of Italian cocktail culture. Speaking at the event, Maurizio Ferri , Director of the Italian Trade Agency, highlighted the initiative’s goal of promoting Italian wines and spirits, featuring brands such as Campari, Aperol and Martini. The experience began with a masterclass hosted by Lara Rawa , founder of Lagos Cocktail Week, exploring five Italian classics: the Negroni, Americano, Bellini, Aperol Spritz and Garibaldi. Guests learned about the Italian aperitif tradition and how individual palates shape cocktail preferences. The evening continued with networking, Italian wine and cocktail tastings, and special guests, including Chef Gibbs and visiting bartenders from Abidjan and Ghana. With music by DJ Exclusive , the event combined cultural exchange, education and entertainment in celebration of Italian cocktail culture. One of the most exciting additions to this year’s festival was the debut of the Lagos Bar Show, a fresh take on the traditional bar hop that brought the spirit of Pan-African collaboration directly into some of Lagos’ most exciting bars. On Tuesday, October 20, Sora Lagos played host to the first guest shift, welcoming the team from Bissa, Abidjan, for an exciting collaboration featuring Dodo Plantain Infused Rum. The following evening, Wednesday, October 21, the spotlight shifted to Praia Lagos, where bartenders from Accra’s Front/Back and No. 19 Bar & Restaurant brought a taste of Ghana’s cocktail scene to Lagos, with Audry Cognac taking centre stage. The guest bartenders took over the bar, creating a selection of signature cocktails with Audry Cognac as their base. Front/Back’s bartenders served the Mantse and Ashanti, while the team from No. 19 Bar & Restaurant presented the Akwaaba, meaning “welcome,” and Nkabom, meaning “togetherness.” Praia Lagos’ bartenders also showcased their creativity with Audry Cognac, serving the Audry Passion Sour and

The experience began with a masterclass hosted by Lara Rawa , founder of Lagos Cocktail Week, exploring five Italian classics: the Negroni, Americano, Bellini, Aperol Spritz and Garibaldi. Guests learned about the Italian aperitif tradition and how individual palates shape cocktail preferences. The evening continued with networking, Italian wine and cocktail tastings, and special guests, including Chef Gibbs and visiting bartenders from Abidjan and Ghana. With music by DJ Exclusive , the event combined cultural exchange, education and entertainment in celebration of Italian cocktail culture. One of the most exciting additions to this year’s festival was the debut of the Lagos Bar Show, a fresh take on the traditional bar hop that brought the spirit of Pan-African collaboration directly into some of Lagos’ most exciting bars. On Tuesday, October 20, Sora Lagos played host to the first guest shift, welcoming the team from Bissa, Abidjan, for an exciting collaboration featuring Dodo Plantain Infused Rum. The following evening, Wednesday, October 21, the spotlight shifted to Praia Lagos, where bartenders from Accra’s Front/Back and No. 19 Bar & Restaurant brought a taste of Ghana’s cocktail scene to Lagos, with Audry Cognac taking centre stage. The guest bartenders took over the bar, creating a selection of signature cocktails with Audry Cognac as their base. Front/Back’s bartenders served the Mantse and Ashanti, while the team from No. 19 Bar & Restaurant presented the Akwaaba, meaning “welcome,” and Nkabom, meaning “togetherness.” Praia Lagos’ bartenders also showcased their creativity with Audry Cognac, serving the Audry Passion Sour and Audry Old Fashioned. The evening drew professional bartenders, mixologists and cocktail enthusiasts, who gathered to support the guest teams and celebrate the culture of bartending and mixology. The lively event combined Ghanaian cocktail influences with Lagos’ vibrant bar scene, creating memorable moments of cultural exchange, collaboration and celebration. Beyond the cocktails and celebrations, Lagos Cocktail Week 2026 also reinforced its commitment to industry growth, knowledge-sharing, and professional development. On Thursday, October 22, the festival’s industry conference took place at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Federal Palace Hotel, Lagos, bringing together bartenders, hospitality entrepreneurs, brand representatives, and key industry stakeholders for conversations about the future of Africa’s cocktail and hospitality landscape. The conference explored the theme “Shaping the Future of Hospitality”. It brought together hospitality professionals and industry stakeholders to explore opportunities and emerging trends across Nigeria’s beverage and hospitality sectors. Discussions covered the business behind the bar, the future of beverage service at Nigerian events, gastro mixology, wine pairings, modern cocktail techniques and the future of mixology in Nigeria. Speakers included Jeremiah George, founder of Liquids by Zen; Emem Udom, founder of Apotheca Mixology ; Folakemi Alli-Balogun, founder of The Wine Club Lagos ; Benedicta Ogar, CEO of Cavodah and founder of SAHA Africa ; Olawuyi Babatunde Abinibi , creative director of Abinibi Events Cottage ; and Captain Gibbs, chef and founder of the Nigerian Food Summit . The conference provided a platform for knowledge-sharing, industry collaboration and conversations on advancing hospitality standards and shaping the future of Nigeria’s cocktail and beverage industry. The excitement reached its peak on October 22 and 23 with the highly anticipated Cocktail Village, transforming the Balmoral Convention Centre at the Federal Palace Hotel, Victoria Island, into a vibrant playground of cocktails, music, entertainment, and unforgettable experiences. Across two exhilarating days, cocktail enthusiasts were treated to unlimited cocktails, immersive brand activations, live performances, and opportunities to discover exciting new flavours, interact with their favourite brands, and connect with fellow lovers of cocktail culture. Adding a competitive edge to the festivities was the crowd-favourite Bar Battle, which saw talented mixologists put their creativity, technical skills, and showmanship to the test in a thrilling contest for the coveted title of Lagos Cocktail Week Champion across three brand-sponsored challenges. In the Absolut Challenge, Onaghise Kingsley Osagie won ₦1 million, while Samuel Olubunmi Ayodele received ₦500,000. The MONIN Challenge saw Valentine Justin take first place with ₦500,000, followed by Benjamin Terna (₦300,000) and Aghama Gabriel (₦200,000). In the Johnnie Walker Challenge, Victoria Chiamaka emerged as Lagos Cocktail Champion, winning ₦1 million, while Aghama Gabriel and Victor Ceasar received ₦200,000 and ₦100,000, respectively, for their innovative serves. Other finalists received ₦200,000 voucher cards redeemable at Legend Supermarket. The competition celebrated the creativity and talent driving Nigeria’s growing mixology industry. The festival came to a spectacular close on Friday, October 23, with the Cocktail Village Grand Finale, bringing together an exciting mix of partner activations, entertainment, and celebratory moments. Adding to the night’s electric atmosphere was an energetic performance by dynamic duo Wanni X Handi, providing a fitting finale to eight days of cocktail-inspired experiences. While the curtains have closed on Lagos Cocktail Week 2026, the impact of this year’s edition extends far beyond the festivities. Through its celebration of African talent, cross-border collaborations, and commitment to industry development, the festival continues to strengthen its position as a leading platform for cocktail culture, creativity, and hospitality innovation across the continent. Lagos Cocktail Week 2026 was proudly supported by Absolut, Casamigos Tequila, Johnnie Walker, Gordon’s, Tanqueray, Lord’s Gin, Natterjack Irish Whiskey, Smirnoff X1, Gold Bar Whiskey, Schweppes, Nestlé Pure Life, West Cork Distillers, Orijin, MONIN, Cutty Sark, Bolt, Eventi Cocktails, Sip Pass, Ocean5 Riviera and Balmoral. Government and Institutional Partners: Lagos State Ministry of Tourism, Arts & Culture, Italian Trade Agency. item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns, in a spectacular downfall for the longtime head of the chipmaker, a vital player in the artificial intelligence boom. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion-dollar company plunging, and the exit of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom, leaves Nvidia without its leather-jacket-clad leader at a crucial time for the sector.

item.title: European security and Ukraine talks top agenda at Dublin summit

item.title: United Airlines wants you to check in, not your chatbot
item.description: United Airlines has become the latest company to slap restrictions on unauthorized third-party AI agents, warning that the bots could make unintended purchases, expose customer data, or bypass checks requiring human acknowledgment. The airline announced restrictions covering both its own digital platforms and indirect access through travel agencies and aggregators, with changes to its booking, ticketing, and distribution policies. United says automated actions could violate aviation regulations, citing the requirement for a human acknowledgment during check-in that bags contain no banned substances. A bot cheerfully ticking the box isn't quite the passenger confirmation it has in mind. And then there is the worry that "sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles." United would also rather customers use its own app than turn third-party assistants loose on its systems. AI agents are pitched as a way to outsource life's minutiae, and it's difficult to navigate the web without tripping over a breathless influencer explaining why you need one, or dozens, or hundreds of virtual personal assistants. The thing is that operating these assistants requires care and thought. Earlier this year, British mathematician Professor Hannah Fry conducted a cautionary experiment in which she gave an AI agent a bank card, and a bit too much agency, to see what it would do. Passwords were coughed up, and some ill-considered purchases were made. Still, as Fry said of the agent, dubbed Cassandra, "don't let her incompetence fool you, because these things are getting better fast." Last month, reports emerged of major US banks blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside accounts and taking actions on behalf of the customer. This month, several UK banks were reported to have followed suit. United stated: "Corporate leaders in the banking and retail industries have taken similar actions regarding AI agents and we encourage others to consider measures that preserve the data and security of their customers and strengthen safety." The Register asked United Airlines how it planned to implement the blocking. There are a few options, including physical biometric confirmation for actions or checking for signs of automated browser driving. Amazon has also moved against unauthorized AI agents, blocking Meta's Muse (the "AI that gets it done," according to Meta's marketing) in September . The airline has yet to respond. ®

item.title: PHOTOS: Nigerian High Commissioner, others present Letters of Credence to Ghanaian President
item.description: President John Dramani Mahama of the Republic of Ghana has received Letters of Credence from the 11 newly appointed Ambassadors and High Commissioners. Diplomats from South Africa, Nigeria, India, Thailand, Lebanon, Australia, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Finland, Slovakia and Sweden presented their letters to the President at Jubilee House, Accra. Addressing the diplomatic representatives, President Mahama reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to deepening diplomatic engagement, strengthening bilateral relations and exploring new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation. He highlighted Ghana’s interest in strengthening its historical, political, cultural and economic ties with partner nations, while calling for greater international collaboration in advancing shared priorities, including Africa’s development, reparatory justice and investment opportunities. item.title: US public workers are fighting to protect their jobs from AI – and some are winning
item.description: As governments adopt AI, workers are gaining ground in how it’s used and securing safeguards against its harms In the shadow of Silicon Valley, workers for the city of Oakland, California, worry the region will deploy AI systems that could increase surveillance and inaccurately evaluate their performance. Pushing for protections to ensure workers won’t be laid off or disciplined by AI, their union overwhelmingly voted on 22 October to authorize a strike, with 94.1% in favor. “We just want the city administration to really be intentional about how it’s engaging with AI products,” said Julian Ware, an Oakland spatial data administrator and member of International Federation of Professional and Technical Engineers Local 21. “Sometimes with a fancy new toy, it actually costs more, it’s more difficult to implement and the results are not as good.” Continue reading...

item.title: I used the Vaonis Vespera 3 for weeks and here’s who I would recommend it to — full review
item.description: null I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money. Yet I found myself increasingly impressed by what the Vespera 3 could achieve, particularly when I returned to the same object over several nights. The images were sharp, the colors were excellent and I almost never had to think about the battery. The Vespera III weighs 13 lbs (6 kg) including the tripod. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) That doesn’t mean the experience was flawless. I sometimes spent longer than I’d have liked waiting for the telescope to get ready, but once it began photographing the sky, the Vespera 3 reminded me why I love smart telescopes so much. Why I kept returning to the same objects over several nights The Vespera 3 uses a Sony IMX585 sensor to produce 8.3MP images. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One of my favorite things about smart telescopes is watching a photograph develop as more light is collected. What begins as a fairly ordinary patch of stars gradually becomes something much more interesting. First a faint cloud of gas appears, then more structure emerges, and eventually you have an image that, only a few short years ago, would have been difficult to capture without specialist equipment. With the Vespera 3, I spent several nights photographing the Pleiades (M45), the famous star cluster in Taurus. The Pleiades make an excellent subject for testing a telescope because the stars are bright, but the surrounding nebulosity is much harder to capture convincingly. The Singularity app used to control Vespera 3 stacks each image as it goes, but keeps them in sight as an optional time-lapse, so you can see exactly why you’re spending so much time on one object. Even better, the Vespera 3’s PerseverENS feature lets you add data to an existing observation over multiple nights (it’s actually called multi-night observation in the app). Instead of having to call it a night or start again every time the weather interrupts an imaging session, you can return to a target and continue building the image over weeks — or years. This is excellent for faint nebulas, but also for anyone who lives somewhere with unpredictable weather. item.dc:creator: Jamie Carter
item.content:encoded: null I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money. Yet I found myself increasingly impressed by what the Vespera 3 could achieve, particularly when I returned to the same object over several nights. The images were sharp, the colors were excellent and I almost never had to think about the battery. The Vespera III weighs 13 lbs (6 kg) including the tripod. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) That doesn’t mean the experience was flawless. I sometimes spent longer than I’d have liked waiting for the telescope to get ready, but once it began photographing the sky, the Vespera 3 reminded me why I love smart telescopes so much. Why I kept returning to the same objects over several nights The Vespera 3 uses a Sony IMX585 sensor to produce 8.3MP images. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One of my favorite things about smart telescopes is watching a photograph develop as more light is collected. What begins as a fairly ordinary patch of stars gradually becomes something much more interesting. First a faint cloud of gas appears, then more structure emerges, and eventually you have an image that, only a few short years ago, would have been difficult to capture without specialist equipment. With the Vespera 3, I spent several nights photographing the Pleiades (M45), the famous star cluster in Taurus. The Pleiades make an excellent subject for testing a telescope because the stars are bright, but the surrounding nebulosity is much harder to capture convincingly. The Singularity app used to control Vespera 3 stacks each image as it goes, but keeps them in sight as an optional time-lapse, so you can see exactly why you’re spending so much time on one object. Even better, the Vespera 3’s PerseverENS feature lets you add data to an existing observation over multiple nights (it’s actually called multi-night observation in the app). Instead of having to call it a night or start again every time the weather interrupts an imaging session, you can return to a target and continue building the image over weeks — or years. This is excellent for faint nebulas, but also for anyone who lives somewhere with unpredictable weather. The Vespera 3 also has CovalENS, Vaonis’s mosaic imaging system, which captures adjacent sections of sky to produce a larger image. That’s helpful for objects such as the Pleiades and large nebulas, which occupy a substantial area of the sky. Mosaics inevitably take longer than conventional images — if it images six sections of the night sky, it takes six times longer for the same image quality — but they also make the telescope more versatile than its native field of view (2.5 x 1.4 degrees) might suggest. I was impressed by what it captured from an urban location Various filters can be popped in and out of the lens. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Smart telescopes are particularly useful for people living under light-polluted skies. A conventional optical telescope can show you the moon, the planets and some brighter star clusters, but faint nebulas are largely out of reach. The Vespera 3 tackles that problem by taking repeated short exposures and combining them automatically. As the exposures accumulate, faint details become clearer, and the image becomes less noisy. I photographed the Orion Nebula (M42), one of the most rewarding deep-sky targets for almost any telescope. Its bright central region makes it a quick capture, but the surrounding clouds of gas give a camera plenty more to uncover. The color in M42 via the Vespera 3 was particularly striking: stars looked sharp, the background was pleasingly clean, but the colors had a richness you don’t always see from less expensive models. The branded adjustable tripod provides a stable platform. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) The Vespera 3 uses a 50mm refractor telescope and an 8.3-megapixel Sony IMX585 camera sensor. Those specifications are identical to the Vespera 2, but the Vespera 3 has a new optical system, which uses four lenses in three groups, including two extra-low-dispersion elements. Vaonis has also introduced internal baffling to reduce unwanted reflections from nearby artificial lights. For urban astronomers, every little helps. I wouldn’t claim that the Vespera 3 makes dark skies unnecessary. It doesn’t — and if you do take a trip to dark skies with the Vespera 3, your images will improve — but it can produce extremely satisfying images even from a city. The main chassis of the telescope sports a large logo. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) For anyone who wants more control over their images, the Vespera 3 also saves lossless TIFF files that can be exported to a PC or Mac using a USB-C cable. That means you can take the images into your preferred editing software for further processing, rather than relying entirely on the results produced by the Singularity app. The supplied tripod is sturdy and dependable. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) I wish choosing what to photograph was more intuitive There’s something wonderfully simple about looking at a map of the night sky, spotting an interesting object and tapping it to point your scope in that direction. It’s one of the reasons I enjoy using Seestar smart telescopes. I did miss that experience with the Vespera 3. Vaonis’s Singularity app has an extensive catalog of galaxies, nebulas, star clusters and other targets, but I found myself browsing lists when I’d rather have been exploring an interactive sky chart. There is a section devoted to constellations, which initially got my hopes up. I thought it might allow me to photograph an entire constellation, capturing its familiar star pattern as a wide-field image. Sadly not — each constellation has a diagram showing where the catalog’s deep-sky objects are located. That’s useful if you already know what you’re looking for, but it isn’t the same as being able to see the sky overhead and choose a target visually. However, the telescope can still find and photograph the objects in its catalog, and the automated tracking works well once you’ve made your choice. It takes a while to get started A fabric canopy between the tripod’s legs keeps accessories close at hand. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) That smart telescopes give you instant gratification is something of a selling point — but it’s also a myth. Yes, they save an enormous amount of work compared with traditional astrophotography equipment. There’s no separate tracking mount to align, no camera to attach and no laptop required to control the imaging process. However, automation doesn’t necessarily mean instant results. For example, every time the Vespera 3 is switched on, it needs to establish its position by identifying stars overhead. Its Star Zone Search and autofocus procedure took around five minutes, with a percentage displayed in the app to show how far it had progressed. That’s not an unreasonable wait for a sophisticated astronomical instrument, but it felt a little drawn-out when I was eager to begin photographing something. If there are clouds, expect it to take much longer. Once the Vespera 3 had aligned itself, I could choose a target and leave the telescope to work. The optical arm moved into position, the camera began collecting exposures and an image gradually appeared on my smartphone. I was less impressed by the tou

item.title: Satellite snaps rare birds-eye view of the ISS | Space photo of the day for Nov. 12, 2026
item.description: null A satellite looks down at the International Space Station in orbit. (Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system. HEO doesn't build the satellites that take these photos; rather, the company's software tasks the spacecraft to image targets as they come into range. This great photo of the ISS from above, for example, was taken by a satellite operated by BlackSky, a Virginia-based company that holds a non-Earth imaging agreement with HEO . So far, HEO and its partners have captured imagery of a variety of spacecraft in orbit, including the ISS, China's Tiangong space station and the European Space Agency's ERS-2 satellite (while it was hurtling back to Earth in 2024). Why is it incredible? While it might seem that satellites are just hovering above Earth, the space station and other spacecraft in LEO are hurtling through space at roughly 17,500 mph (28,160 kph), hundreds of miles above our planet's surface. A snapshot of a satellite from above is therefore far from mundane. Rather, it requires incredible coordination and technical skill; satellite operators must know precisely when their target will present itself, and their equipment must be capable of getting the shot.

item.title: Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List
item.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram If Olamide ‘s ‘ Burukutu ‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space . Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project. Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu . Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range. The newly revealed tracklist opens with “ Elohim ” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “ Skoskola “, “ Say Less “, the lead anthem “ Burukutu “, and “ Alujon ” rounding out the first half. The second half picks up the tempo with “ Mbiri “, the collaborative track “ Jaiye ” featuring vocalist Fola , followed by “ Oshey “, “ Ring “, and the closing record “ Jogor “. Keeping features remarkably streamlined, the album highlights a targeted guest appearance from Nigerian singer Fola, allowing Olamide’s distinctive penmanship and vocal direction to take centre stage across the entire tracklist. The official 10-track tracklist for Olamide’s album Time & Space, featuring lead single Burukutu and a guest appearance by Fola. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram This forthcoming release arrives as the direct successor to his self-titled studio album, Olamidé , which dropped in June 2025 with a sprawling 17-track setup featuring heavyweights like Wizkid . Where that previous body of work leaned into massive collaborative constellations, Time & Space scales back into a more intimate, focused exploration of sound, anchored tightly by the creative vision of the YBNL boss himself. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue. The post Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: The Beatz Awards Unveils 2026 Nominees, Marking 11 Years Of Celebrating The Creators Behind The Sound
item.description: The Beatz Awards has announced the nominees for its 11th Edition, celebrating 11 years of recognising the creative minds, technical professionals and business stakeholders whose work drives Nigeria’s music industry and the wider African music ecosystem. Guided by the theme “ Behind the Beat, Beyond the Beat ”, this year’s nominations span music production, songwriting, sound engineering, music video direction, broadcasting, digital music platforms, artist management and the wider business of music. The awards spotlight the people and teams whose contributions often happen beyond the public gaze but remain essential to the creation, distribution and commercial success of music. The production categories feature leading and emerging talents across Afro Pop, Afro Beat, Afro R&B, Afro Hip-Hop, Afro Highlife, Afro Soul, Afro Dancehall and Afro Gospel. Nominees include Magicsticks, Sarz, Niphkeys, Ozedikus, Fresh VDM, Ragee, Saszy Afroshii, Tems, Dunnie, Bloody Civilian and rising producers Hunkie Beats, Juixce, Decs, Lekaa Beats, JJAY, Jhay2unez and Shallythechampion. The 2026 field also recognises technical and creative excellence in mixing and mastering, music video direction and songwriting. Broadcasting, media and music business categories include radio and television stations, OAPs, DJs, artist managers, record labels, blogs, online music platforms, A&Rs, live bands and entertainment lawyers. “ Behind every hit record is a team the audience never sees. Our nominees are the engine of African music.” — Elijah John , Founder & Executive Producer, The Beatz Awards Public voting opens on 21 October and runs until 16 November 2026. Music fans and supporters are encouraged to visit the official website, explore the nominees and cast their votes. The 11th Edition awards ceremony will take place on 21 November 2026 at Shell Hall, MUSON Centre, Onikan, Lagos. item.title: Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 enter their 'permanently vulnerable' era
item.description: Microsoft has warned customers still clinging to Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 to consider the software "permanently vulnerable" as November's security fixes arrive for Subscription Edition (SE) alone. The warning appears in the release documentation for November's Exchange Server SE security update. Looking for Exchange 2016 and 2019 information? Tough. Microsoft stated: "Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are no longer tested for vulnerabilities and there are no updates released. If you are using those versions of Exchange, you should consider them permanently vulnerable [Microsoft's emphasis] and should upgrade your organization immediately." You have been warned. Support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 ended on October 14, 2025, but the company announced an Extended Security Updates (ESU) program in July 2025. The plan was that this program would end on April 14, 2026, by which time customers would surely have made the jump to a later or online version, right? The company said: "This period will not be extended past April 2026 (you do not need to ask)." And... of course it was. As April 2026 rolled around, and it became clear that some customers were still stubbornly sticking with the old versions, Microsoft did the equivalent of heaving an exasperated sigh and offered another six months of paid security updates. Those final weeks also brought a separate treat: a Windows Server update breaking Exchange Server . This time it was serious. Microsoft released the final Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 security updates on October 13. No more patches, no more vulnerability testing, and apparently no more reprieves. According to Microsoft's Security Update Guide , the November update fixed nine vulnerabilities in Exchange Server SE, including a critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-118207. Microsoft isn't testing earlier versions of Exchange for the vulnerabilities. ®

item.title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
item.description: Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days . Now, Google is ready to take another swing at " intelligent eyewear " for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they're no impulse buy. These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered. Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn't told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea. Read full article Comments

item.title: ICRC 'currently classifying the highest number of armed conflicts since the Second World War
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Mirjana Spoljaric. “You may consider war a human condition,” argues Spoljaric. “But brutality, barbarity, is not a human condition.” Her warning recalls the fundamental premise of the 1949 Geneva Conventions: even in war, there can be no lawless space, and certain red lines must never be crossed.

item.title: France's social safety net: Can it afford to be so generous?
item.description: Created in the aftermath of World War II, France's social security system has become one of the pillars of French society, providing everything from healthcare and family benefits to pensions. But with an ageing population and mounting deficits, this ambitious model is facing a major financial test. We look at how the system works, why it is so deeply valued by the French and whether the country can afford to keep its promise of protecting everyone – from cradle to grave.

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive
item.description: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of the company, following the revelation of his affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy and reports of a relationship with another woman who was a company employee. In a Form 8-K [PDF] filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the GPU maker disclosed that it accepted the resignation of Huang, whom it identified as Jen-Hsun Huang, on November 11, effective immediately. He is being replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim leader while the board conducts a search for a new CEO. Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as president, CEO, and a member of the board of directors ever since, led the GPU maker to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, hitting a hit peak of over $5.5 trillion earlier this year. His position became untenable following an investigation by the company's board after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a romantic relationship with a woman the US authorities suspected as a Chinese spy. Reports later surfaced this week of a second alleged affair with an employee of the company itself, reported by the New York Times as being with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. A two-week downfall News of the scandal first broke barely a couple of weeks ago, on October 29, when claims surfaced that Huang had been the target of an espionage plot involving a Chinese businesswoman working for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed which was a customer of Nvidia. According to the New York Times , US intelligence had reason to believe the woman, Alice Huang, was recruited to gather information about Nvidia and its operations for the Beijing government. Megaspeed also faces claims it was illicitly shipping Nvidia products to China, in violation of US export controls. Any relationship between Huang and a Chinese operative would be enormously concerning, as the US has been trying to keep advanced technology for AI out of the hands of the country, allegedly for security reasons, fearing it might be used for military purposes. For its part, Beijing rejects the spying allegations, saying they are part of a smear campaign against China. Shortly after Nvidia’s board announced it was investigating Huang, he sent an email to Nvidia staff apologizing and confessing to having an affair, though he did not explicitly name Alice Huang in his public apology. It seemed like the leather-jacketed leader might just hang on, since it was difficult to imagine anyone other than him leading the company after all this time. But Nvidia’s shares fell 4.3 percent on November 9 and a further 5.5 percent the following day, wiping around $430 billion off its market value, amid all the speculation. Then the claim emerged regarding a second affair, with an employee at Nvidia who reported to him, and many commentators took it as a sign the game was up. Huang resigned the same day the news broke. Indecision ahead Now

Indecision ahead Now the speculation starts over who will take over the reins at Nvidia, but Huang could prove a tough act to follow. He is said to have recognized early on the potential for taking the number-crunching capabilities of graphics processors and putting them to use at accelerating AI processing, and Nvidia’s position today as the leading AI hardware firm is thanks to that bet. “The sudden resignation of Jensen Huang is about more than succession at the world’s most important AI chipmaker, Nvidia’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom,” says Forrester VP and group research director Stephanie Balaouras. If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience, she adds. But if its stock or financing relationships remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragility of the AI bubble. “In the near term, the board did the sensible thing and reached for a steward. Colette Kress knows every number in that order book,” commented Mark Malek, CIO at financial services firm Siebert Financial. “It does NOT settle the stock. Interim means the real decision is still ahead, the investigations are still open, and next week’s earnings call just became the most important in the company’s history,” he added. ®

item.title: ‘To them, we’re just NPCs’: the artists and activists challenging Trump’s video game propaganda
item.description: Order a Diet Coke or invade Iran – that’s the choice facing the US president in one of several satirical games, as designers turn the gamification of politics back on the White House In early September, the Trump White House announced a surprising new addition to its official website. Named simply Arcade , it is a collection of browser games based on classic titles such as Flappy Bird, Snake, and Tetris, but re-tuned as flagrant works of political propaganda. Designed to court reactionary gamers, they push the administration’s policies on immigration and other hot-button issues, while dehumanising their targets. There have recently been some new additions: a Temple Run clone named Red Scare about crossing the “ration market” and escaping the Democratic Socialists of America, and another simple item-matching game about the threat of socialism. In the midst of increasing fuel, utility and grocery prices thanks to the Iran war, these were naked attempts to distract voters by appealing to their video game nostalgia. After an explosion of news coverage, Arcade caught the attention of the games industry. The Tetris Company warned on social media that it “took copyright infringement very seriously.” Days later, the game was removed from the White House site. However, aside from a March 2026 statement from the Pokémon Company condemning the White House for using its characters in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) propaganda, major video game companies have been relatively silent in the face of the administration’s widespread usage of their IP. Continue reading...

item.title: Pierre Sage’s failure to fix defensive flaws leaves Crystal Palace seeking new solution
item.description: A losing run, set-piece struggles and a call for help led Steve Parish to cut ties with the manager after five months The moment that summed up Crystal Palace’s season under Pierre Sage came five minutes before half-time at Selhurst Park on Sunday. After Palace had gone close to taking the lead on numerous occasions against Liverpool, the Frenchman must have feared the worst when Alexis Mac Allister headed in from a soft free-kick conceded by Jefferson Lerma. The TV cameras immediately panned to Steve Parish in the stands. After the Palace chair removed his hands from in front of his eyes, his expression said everything you needed to know. The only surprise was that Sage had to wait until Thursday before his inevitable fate was confirmed . Not since the start of the 2017-18 season, after Frank de Boer was appointed as Palace’s first permanent foreign manager and sacked after five matches, have the club found themselves bottom. In their record 14th consecutive season in the top flight, and with preliminary work having started on building a new £200m main stand despite major doubts over funding, Palace cannot afford to be relegated. Continue reading...

item.title: Vast data dump from Euclid space telescope reveals stunning galaxies
item.description: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The European Space Agency has just released a vast batch of observations of the sky captured by the Euclid space telescope. Launched in 2023, the telescope is currently on a six-year mission to image about one-third of the sky to build the most detailed 3D map of the cosmos ever created . The latest observations – catchily titled DR1-Foundation – cover an area of the sky as big as 9500 full moons. The collection includes 900 million galaxies. The mosaic of 740 images at the top of the article, collected in autumn 2024 and spring 2025, covers 367 square degrees of the northern sky. At full resolution, this snapshot runs to 500 gigapixels. Advertisement The bright oval in the lower left portion of the patchwork image is the spiral galaxy Messier 81, which is some 12 million light years from Earth. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Messier 81 in greater detail, along with part of the M81 group of galaxies that also bears its name – an honour bestowed on it as the largest galaxy of the bunch. To the lower left is the smaller galaxy NGC 3077, and the patches of wispy blue cloud throughout the images are galactic cirrus, which are actually in the foreground and part of our own home galaxy. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO Here, Messier 81 is shown in even greater detail, in an image taken at the full resolution available to Euclid. The haze dominating the right side of the frame is the disc of Messier 81, inside which individual stars are visible. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO This hazy galaxy is NGC 1291, around 33 million light years away. The image was made from two taken by Euclid and then cropped. In the background, even more distant galaxies are visible – the furthest away of which show up in red. Stars are still actively forming within NGC 1291, and can be seen as small blue-hued dots. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Abell 3128, a cluster of hundreds of galaxies lying around 800 million light years away. The cluster is home to a diverse array of galaxies, including whirling spirals and fuzzy ellipticals. In the centre of the image is a strong gravitational lens, where the light travelling to us from a more distant galaxy has been warped by a massive object in the foreground.

item.title: The 'eclipse of the century' will plunge these 8 wonders of the Roman Empire into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027
item.description: null Ancient Egyptian temples will inevitably dominate the story of the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . After all, the path of totality crosses Luxor, home to Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the ancient world's most famous monuments. But follow the moon 's shadow west and another ancient civilization comes into view. Before reaching Egypt, totality will sweep across the Mediterranean and North Africa, passing over an extraordinary collection of Roman cities, fortresses, theaters, temples and triumphal arches. Many lie within what became Rome's North African provinces, a region that produced some of the empire's wealthiest and most impressive cities. From beachside Baelo Claudia in Spain and military Tamuda in Morocco to Timgad and Djémila in Algeria and the jaw-dropping El Jem Amphitheater in Tunisia, Roman ruins will experience between two and more than five minutes of darkness — creating extraordinary possibilities for eclipse chasers and photographers. Here are some of the best places to watch the moon's shadow cross what was once the Roman Empire. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date . 1. Baelo Claudia, Spain Baelo Claudia's Roman ruins overlook Bolonia beach and the Strait of Gibraltar. (Image credit: Andrea Pucci via Getty Images) Location: near Tarifa, Andalucía, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:44 a.m. CEST; 4 minutes, 31 seconds Historical cloud cover: 12% Altitude of the sun: 37 degrees above east Roman ruins, an Atlantic beach and the mountains of Africa could all share the frame with the eclipsed sun at Baelo Claudia. Founded in the second century B.C., this remarkably well-preserved Roman city near Bolonia beach includes a forum, basilica, theater, temples, baths and a decumanus maximus (east-west street), all set against forested hills and a vast coastal sand dune. For photographers, the possibilities are exceptional — columns and temples may provide an ancient foreground, while wider compositions could incorporate the beach and dunes. On particularly clear days, Morocco is visible across the Strait of Gibraltar — potentially putting Roman ruins, two continents and a total solar eclipse into one extraordinary scene. 2. Málaga Roman Theatre, Spain The Roman Theatre at the foot of the Málaga Alcazaba dates back to the 1st century BC. (Image credit: Manfred Gottschalk via Getty Images) Location: Málaga, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:48 a.m. CEST; 1 minute, 57 seconds Historical cloud cover: 9% Altitude of the sun: 39 degrees above east Few eclipse locations can offer two civilizations in the same photograph. Málaga's Roman Theatre was built in the first century B.C., when the city was part of the Roman province of Hispania, and today sits directly beneath the Alcazaba, the imposing Muslim-era palace-fortress that dominates the hillside above. item.dc:creator: Jamie Carter
item.content:encoded: null Ancient Egyptian temples will inevitably dominate the story of the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . After all, the path of totality crosses Luxor, home to Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the ancient world's most famous monuments. But follow the moon 's shadow west and another ancient civilization comes into view. Before reaching Egypt, totality will sweep across the Mediterranean and North Africa, passing over an extraordinary collection of Roman cities, fortresses, theaters, temples and triumphal arches. Many lie within what became Rome's North African provinces, a region that produced some of the empire's wealthiest and most impressive cities. From beachside Baelo Claudia in Spain and military Tamuda in Morocco to Timgad and Djémila in Algeria and the jaw-dropping El Jem Amphitheater in Tunisia, Roman ruins will experience between two and more than five minutes of darkness — creating extraordinary possibilities for eclipse chasers and photographers. Here are some of the best places to watch the moon's shadow cross what was once the Roman Empire. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date . 1. Baelo Claudia, Spain Baelo Claudia's Roman ruins overlook Bolonia beach and the Strait of Gibraltar. (Image credit: Andrea Pucci via Getty Images) Location: near Tarifa, Andalucía, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:44 a.m. CEST; 4 minutes, 31 seconds Historical cloud cover: 12% Altitude of the sun: 37 degrees above east Roman ruins, an Atlantic beach and the mountains of Africa could all share the frame with the eclipsed sun at Baelo Claudia. Founded in the second century B.C., this remarkably well-preserved Roman city near Bolonia beach includes a forum, basilica, theater, temples, baths and a decumanus maximus (east-west street), all set against forested hills and a vast coastal sand dune. For photographers, the possibilities are exceptional — columns and temples may provide an ancient foreground, while wider compositions could incorporate the beach and dunes. On particularly clear days, Morocco is visible across the Strait of Gibraltar — potentially putting Roman ruins, two continents and a total solar eclipse into one extraordinary scene. 2. Málaga Roman Theatre, Spain The Roman Theatre at the foot of the Málaga Alcazaba dates back to the 1st century BC. (Image credit: Manfred Gottschalk via Getty Images) Location: Málaga, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:48 a.m. CEST; 1 minute, 57 seconds Historical cloud cover: 9% Altitude of the sun: 39 degrees above east Few eclipse locations can offer two civilizations in the same photograph. Málaga's Roman Theatre was built in the first century B.C., when the city was part of the Roman province of Hispania, and today sits directly beneath the Alcazaba, the imposing Muslim-era palace-fortress that dominates the hillside above. Although its totality is considerably shorter than locations farther south, the photographic possibilities are compelling. From a carefully chosen position, it may be possible to frame the darkened sun with the theater's ancient stonework and the walls of the Alcazaba rising behind it. Another major advantage for eclipse chasers is that this extraordinary historical setting sits in the heart of Málaga, making it one of the most accessible ancient sites on the path of totality. 3. Tamuda, Morocco The ruins of Tamuda near Tétouan preserve a Roman military fortress. (Image credit: Carole Raddato via Wikipedia CC BY-SA 2.0 ) Location: Tétouan, Morocco Start of totality and duration: 08:45 a.m. GMT; 4 minutes, 51 seconds Historical cloud cover: 14% Altitude of sun: 38 degrees above east-southeast Long before the Romans arrived in northern Morocco, Tamuda was already a thriving Mauretanian settlement. Founded around the third century B.C. in the Martil Valley, near modern Tétouan, the Romans established a fortified military camp here in the first century A.D., whose massive stone walls remain the defining feature of this archaeological site. Tamuda combines long totality, promising weather and an atmospheric archaeological foreground — yet remains far less famous than the Roman sites across the Strait of Gibraltar. 4. Timgad, Algeria The Roman Arch of Timgad, Algeria. (Image credit: Antonio Ciufo via Getty Images) Location: near Batna, Algeria Start of totality and duration: 10:01 a.m. CET; 5 minutes, 20 seconds Historical cloud cover: 5% Altitude of sun: 51 degrees above east-southeast Few places in the 2027 path of totality combine ancient architecture and long totality quite like Timgad. Founded around A.D. 100 as the Roman colony of Thamugadi, this remarkably well-preserved city sits on an open plateau at the foot of Algeria's Aurès Mountains. Its grid of streets, forum, theater, temples, baths and columns survives alongside its most famous monument, the three-arched gateway traditionally known as the Arch of Trajan. A relatively high sun will make close architectural compositions challenging, but Timgad's wide-open site provides plenty of possibilities for carefully planned wide-angle images. 5. Lambaesis, Algeria Arch of Commodus at the Roman site of Lambaesis, Algeria. (Image credit: Ethel Davies / robertharding via Getty Images) Location: near Batna, Algeria Start of totality and duration: 10:01 a.m. CET; 5 minutes, 20 seconds Historical cloud cover: 5% Altitude of sun: 51 degrees above east-southeast Just 12—15 miles (20—25 km) west of Timgad lies its military counterpart. Lambaesis was the principal base of Rome's Legio III Augusta, the legion that helped secure Rome's African Empire. Rather than an entire gridded colonial city, the attraction here is monumental military architecture, most notably the imposing remains of the heart of the fortress. The eclipse circumstances are almost identical to nearby Timgad, with more than five minutes of totality and historically excellent prospects for clear skies. Scout both sites beforehand, study where the sun will stand above the ruins, and decide which offers the strongest alignment — and the easiest access — on eclipse morning. 6. Djémila, Algeria The mountain setting of Djémila, ancient Cuicul, could provide a dramatic backdrop to just over two minutes of totality. (Image credit: Nirian via Getty Images) Location: Djémila, Algeria Start of totality and duration: 10:02 a.m. CET; 2 minutes, 2 seconds Historical cloud cover: 11% Altitude of eclipsed sun: 50 degrees above east-southeast Djémila trades a long eclipse for one of the most spectacular settings on the path of totality. Known to the Romans as Cuicul, this exceptionally well-preserved city was built in mountainous terrain around 2,950 feet (900 meters) above sea level — an unusual setting for a Roman settlement — and its ruins include temples, forums, houses, baths, arches and a theater. The surrounding green hills and mountains give eclipse photographers a very different backdrop from the flatter, more arid landscapes farther south. The catch is totality, which is significantly shorter than at other Roman ruins. 7. Sbeitla, Tunisia The Roman temples of ancient Sufetula at Sbeitla, Tunisia. (Image credit: Renee Vititoe via Getty Images) Location: Kasserine, Tunisia Start of totality and duration: 10:06 a.m. CET; 5 minutes, 19 seconds Historical cloud cover: 4% Altitude of sun: 54 degrees above east-southeast Sbeitla could be one of the great archaeological settings for the 2027 eclipse. Known in Roman times as Sufetula, the city prospered under Roman rule and today contains some of Tunisia's most impressive ancient ruins. Its centerpiece is an unusual group of three remarkably well-preserved temples dedicated to Jupiter, Juno and Minerva, standing above the forum and reached through the monumental Arch of Antoninus Pius. item.title: Quantum leap: IBM plans to scale beyond 1,000 qubits in 2027 with Nighthawk r3 processor
item.description: IBM has unveiled the Nighthawk r3, an upcoming next-gen quantum processor that will feature 520 qubits, as another step towards a planned fault-tolerant quantum system it hopes to launch in 2029. Big Blue's current Nighthawk r2 was only made available in September and features 120 quantum bits (qubits) capable of handling circuits using 7,500 operations. Its successor, IBM claims, will have more than four times as many qubits and execute 10,000 quantum operations to tackle larger, more complex problems while maintaining the same speed and accuracy. Nighthawk r3 is slated to arrive in 2027, when Big Blue plans to link two of the quantum processors into a single system with more than 1,000 qubits. IBM said applications increasingly require circuits executing thousands of quantum operations on approximately 100 qubits or more, speeding up collection of the millions or billions of samples needed to perform complex computations. Speed determines whether such demanding workloads can be completed in practical timeframes and at a reasonable cost. The new quantum processor will feature 10 chip-to-chip interconnects, called l-couplers, designed for linking together processors that it will use to enable a single 1,040-qubit system. This tech was tested using Nighthawk r1 processors . IBM previously outlined its goal of reaching reliable error correcting territory in 2029 with a quantum processor codenamed Starling. Now it intends for this to be the world’s first fault-tolerant quantum computer , capable of running quantum circuits comprising 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits. This is an ambitious goal, considering fault-tolerant quantum technology always seems to be at least a decade away, despite numerous breakthroughs and technology introductions. However, some in the technology industry believe the odds on a working system are shortening , given the increased activity around making encryption ready with support for quantum-resistant algorithms. Then again, a professor at the University of Auckland New Zealand famously claimed last year that quantum computers hadn't so far managed to factor any number greater than 21 without cheating. IBM presented a framework for Starling in a 2025 paper outlining hardware to implement the improbably named bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity check (qLDPC) error correction codes. These significantly reduce the number of physical qubits needed to store and process quantum information, compared to existing surface codes. Using the architecture in the paper, Big Blue intends to assemble Starling from modules that each contain a quantum memory and logical processing unit (LPU), allowing logic operations on the memory. The modules will have universal adapters letting them connect using l-couplers. IBM is also preparing the way ahead by combining its quantum processors with classical high-performance compute (HPC) systems to research better quantum error correction. item.content:encoded: IBM has unveiled the Nighthawk r3, an upcoming next-gen quantum processor that will feature 520 qubits, as another step towards a planned fault-tolerant quantum system it hopes to launch in 2029. Big Blue's current Nighthawk r2 was only made available in September and features 120 quantum bits (qubits) capable of handling circuits using 7,500 operations. Its successor, IBM claims, will have more than four times as many qubits and execute 10,000 quantum operations to tackle larger, more complex problems while maintaining the same speed and accuracy. Nighthawk r3 is slated to arrive in 2027, when Big Blue plans to link two of the quantum processors into a single system with more than 1,000 qubits. IBM said applications increasingly require circuits executing thousands of quantum operations on approximately 100 qubits or more, speeding up collection of the millions or billions of samples needed to perform complex computations. Speed determines whether such demanding workloads can be completed in practical timeframes and at a reasonable cost. The new quantum processor will feature 10 chip-to-chip interconnects, called l-couplers, designed for linking together processors that it will use to enable a single 1,040-qubit system. This tech was tested using Nighthawk r1 processors . IBM previously outlined its goal of reaching reliable error correcting territory in 2029 with a quantum processor codenamed Starling. Now it intends for this to be the world’s first fault-tolerant quantum computer , capable of running quantum circuits comprising 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits. This is an ambitious goal, considering fault-tolerant quantum technology always seems to be at least a decade away, despite numerous breakthroughs and technology introductions. However, some in the technology industry believe the odds on a working system are shortening , given the increased activity around making encryption ready with support for quantum-resistant algorithms. Then again, a professor at the University of Auckland New Zealand famously claimed last year that quantum computers hadn't so far managed to factor any number greater than 21 without cheating. IBM presented a framework for Starling in a 2025 paper outlining hardware to implement the improbably named bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity check (qLDPC) error correction codes. These significantly reduce the number of physical qubits needed to store and process quantum information, compared to existing surface codes. Using the architecture in the paper, Big Blue intends to assemble Starling from modules that each contain a quantum memory and logical processing unit (LPU), allowing logic operations on the memory. The modules will have universal adapters letting them connect using l-couplers. IBM is also preparing the way ahead by combining its quantum processors with classical high-performance compute (HPC) systems to research better quantum error correction. Last week, Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) in the US announced such a system , combining an IBM Quantum System Two with Nighthawk r2 quantum processors and Umbra, powered by AMD 5th Gen Epyc CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPU accelerators. IBM also has a partnership with Japan's RIKEN scientific research institute under which an IBM Quantum System Two has been integrated with the Fugaku Arm-based supercomputer, once the most powerful system in the world. ®

item.title: Archive, 1990: Peter Shilton wins 125th and final cap of record-breaking England career
item.description: 9 July 1990: The goalkeeper’s 20-year international career ends at the Italia 90 World Cup Harry Kane is expected to break the record for England men’s appearances tonight against Croatia at Wembley in the Nations League, overtaking goalkeeper Peter Shilton’s 125 appearances, a record set nearly four decades ago at the World Cup in Italy . Shilton wore the captain’s armband in his final England appearance in the unloved third-place play-off against Italy in Bari. The Three Lions had previously lost on penalties to West Germany in the semi-finals. Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: Explore Hubble Hubble Home Overview About Hubble The History of Hubble Hubble Timeline Why Have a Telescope in Space? Hubble by the Numbers At the Museum FAQs Impact & Benefits Hubble’s Impact & Benefits Science Impacts Cultural Impact Technology Benefits Impact on Human Spaceflight Astro Community Impacts Science Hubble Science Science Themes Science Highlights Science Behind Discoveries Universe Uncovered Hubble’s Partners in Science Hubble & Citizen Science SI & Hubble Science Explore the Night Sky Observatory Hubble Observatory Hubble Design Mission Operations Science Operations Astronaut Missions to Hubble Hubble vs. Webb Hubble vs. Roman Team Hubble Team Career Aspirations Hubble Astronauts Multimedia Images Videos Online Activities e-Books Sonifications Podcasts 3D Hubble Models Lithographs Fact Sheets Posters Hubble on the NASA App Glossary News Hubble News Social Media Media Resources 35th Anniversary More Online Activities 5 min read NASA’s Hubble Offers Cosmic Sampler of Targets for Roman A collage of strong gravitational lenses observed by Hubble, some of which will be followed up by observations with the Roman Space Telescope, which launched in August 2026. Lenses like these will be used to investigate the evolution of galaxies and dark matter. Credit: NASA, ESA, and X. Huang (University of San Francisco); Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Gravitational lensing, first predicted by Albert Einstein, occurs when the gravity of a massive foreground object, such as a galaxy or cluster of galaxies, bends, warps, and magnifies the light from a more distant background object. The effect is similar to that of a giant lens in space that allows astronomers to view objects much farther away than any telescope could see on its own. The lenses in this image formed from the precise alignment of a distant background galaxy with the mass of a foreground galaxy, creating distorted and magnified images of the background galaxy that appear as arcs around the foreground galaxy. Astronomers will use these observations of a large and varied population of gravitational lenses to construct lens models that will help determine how much mass is in the lensing system’s foreground galaxy – and potentially prove or dispel a theory about dark matter. Astronomers study the amount of distortion of the lensed background galaxies to determine the quantity and distribution of mass in the foreground galaxy, including its invisible dark matter. Hubble views the cosmos primarily in visible and ultraviolet light with some infrared coverage, providing a comprehensive, high-resolution view of individual objects. Roman sees primarily infrared light and some visible, over a much larger field of view to create panoramas of the universe. While Hubble gets a better view of individual lenses, Roman will be able to capture more lenses with its wider field-of-view. If Roman finds a particularly interesting lens, researchers may use Hubble to take follow-up observations using its visible and UV prowess for individual objects. With Hubble’s high-resolution imaging and precise models, researchers should also be able to detect small imperfections in these gravitationally lensed galaxy arcs that would indicate the presence of small clumps of dark matter. Researchers could use these previously undetected clumps to confirm the cold dark matter theory, which predicts the existence of many small dark matter clumps of between a million to a billion solar masses. In contrast, the dark matter halo of our Milky Way galaxy is around 1.3 trillion solar masses. By studying Hubble lens images in detail, researchers intend to build a super-intelligence tool to efficiently search similar arcs in the upcoming Roman images. The Hubble images are expected to both yield their own results on dark matter and pave the way for analysis of Roman’s larger sample of lenses. The unique lenses in this image display some of the different characteristics researchers will see as they collect a diverse and numerous assortment of lenses to test in their models. Panel A is an example of an arc-counterarc configuration, in which the lensed background galaxy appears as a duplicated pair of arcs. The lensed galaxy is being magnified by a pair of foreground galaxies whose combined mass bends the light of the background galaxy around them. The diversity of lenses in this image demonstrate some of the characteristics researchers will uncover with Hubble and Roman. Each lens differs significantly from others in the panel. Credit: NASA, ESA, and X. Huang (University of San Francisco); Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) Panel F is an Einstein Ring, in which the alignment of the background galaxy and approximately spherical mass of the foreground lens are so perfectly situated that the lensed galaxy almost fully encircles the foreground galaxy. Panel I shows a quadruply lensed galaxy, in which the background galaxy is replicated four times, appearing as smeared dots around the foreground galaxy. Panel C also shows a quadruply lensed galaxy, with double knots that are most likely strong star-forming regions in the background galaxy. Some of the magnified and warped background galaxies appear blue and some appear red. These bluish arcs indicate young stars, while reddish arcs indicate older stars. Roman and Hubble will explore these differences to better understand how galaxies evolved earlier in the universe. Most of the foreground lensing galaxies are elliptical galaxies, which are older, denser, and more compact. Lensed images of background galaxies only occur when the mass density of the foreground galaxy reaches a critical point. But not all of these foreground galaxies are ellipticals, and researchers can use these differences to explore the evolutionary paths taken by these galaxies. In panel G, the foreground galaxy appears elongated, which may be true or a trick of perspective, and in panels B and F, the foreground galaxies appear to have spiral arms. Panel D’s foreground galaxy has a visible dust lane, which is rare in a lensing galaxy and the kind of detail that Hubble’s sharp, visible-light vision excels at revealing. The lensed background galaxy could be an Einstein Ring, with the dust lane “breaking” our view of the ring. Because infrared light is less obscured by dust, future Roman infrared observations could help determine whether the arcs form a more complete Einstein ring. These strong lenses were first detected with The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument at Kitt Peak. Hubble subsequently observed them, and Roman will take further observations. Images like these are an example of the kinds of collaborative efforts that routinely take place between NASA’s Great Observatories to build a comprehensive picture of the cosmos. As Roman joins the family of large space observatories that includes Hubble, the Chandra X-ray Observatory, and the James Webb Space Telescope, a new window opens onto the universe, revealing sights previously hidden while expanding our cosmic knowledge for all of humanity. item.title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story
item.description: After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’ The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter , which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October. Continue reading...

item.title: 2026 CAF Awards: Date, Venue, Nominees & Everything to Know
item.description: Achraf Hakimi with his trophy after winning African Player of the Year at the 2025 CAF Awards. Photo Credit: CAF/Instagram For the first time in 12 years, Lagos will host the CAF Awards, with the 2026 ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, 2 December. The event, which was originally set for 7 December, will bring together leading African footballers, coaches and teams at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts in Iganmu. Spanning 18 award categories across men’s and women’s football, the 2026 CAF Awards will celebrate the finest players, coaches, national teams, and clubs across the continent while bringing football royalty, Nollywood stars, Afrobeats performers, and fashion insiders together on one red carpet. The 2026 shortlists come with a notable twist for the host nation. No Nigerian player made the ten-man shortlist for the CAF Men’s Player of the Year award—leaving out Super Eagles stars Victor Osimhen and Ademola Lookman alongside Egypt’s Mohamed Salah —and no Nigerian footballer features in the CAF Women’s Player of the Year category either, with three-time Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year winner Chiamaka Nnadozie also absent from the final lists. Chiamaka Nnadozie celebrating her third consecutive Goalkeeper of the Year win at the 2025 CAF Awards. Photo Credit: Chiamaka Nnadozie/Instagram Even so, Nigeria still has four nominations to look forward to on home soil on 2 December. The Super Falcons are nominated for Women’s National Team of the Year alongside Algeria, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Malawi, Mali, Morocco, and South Africa. In the individual women’s categories, Edo Queens and Falconets shot-stopper Christiana Uzoma represents Nigeria on the Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year shortlist, while Nigerian youth internationals Seimeyeha Janet Akekoromowei and Oluwakemi Adegbuyi are both in the running for Women’s Young Player of the Year. Elsewhere, the headline races feature some of the biggest names in global football. Defending winner Achraf Hakimi of Morocco and Paris Saint-Germain leads the CAF Men’s Player of the Year nominees alongside his compatriots Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari , Senegal’s Sadio Mané , Ismaila Sarr , and Pape Gueye , Côte d’Ivoire’s Amad Diallo , Ghana’s Antoine Semenyo , DR Congo’s Yoane Wissa , and South Africa’s Teboho Mokoena . Ademola Lookman celebrating his Men’s Player of the Year victory at the 2024 CAF Awards. Photo Credit: Ademola Lookman/Instagram Over in the CAF Women’s Player of the Year race, Zambia’s Barbra Banda and Malawi’s Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga headline a competitive ten-player shortlist that also includes South Africa’s Thembi Kgatlana, Ghana’s Portia Boakye , Algeria’s Marine Dafeur, Morocco’s Hanan Ait El Haj , and Cameroon trio Marie Ngah Manga , Michaely Bihina , and Monique Ngock . Other major honours on the night include Men’s and Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year, Interclub Player of the Year, Coach of the Year, Young Player of the Year, National Team of
